SLATEPORT for his pet, PEEKO.\pThat old sea dog, he must really love
that PEEKO.$

replies.text: Peeko has a personal sailor doing the shopping. I am choosing to admire this arrangement rather than become jealous.
He puts real effort into caring for Peeko. That says rather more about their bond than a grand introduction would.
He knows what his partner needs and goes out to get it. I like that.
I wonder whether Peeko recognizes the sound of the bags when he gets home.
That is a very affectionate reason to make a shopping trip. I hope he remembers to get something for himself too.
A celebrated seafarer, now on an important supply mission for one bird. I think his priorities are excellent.
It is nice to hear a grand old sailor talked about in terms of someone he looks after.
A sea trip for the right supplies makes sense if you know exactly what you are looking for. Peeko sounds well provided for.
Love can look like knowing what to bring home. I like that version of the story.
I hope Peeko approves of his purchases. There is clearly a great deal of devotion behind the selection.
I would love a picture of the moment he returns and Peeko sees what he brought.

contexts.subject: A child wants to travel with Pokemon when older.

RustboroCity_Text_WowYouHavePokemon.text: Wow, you have POKéMON with you, too.\pWhen I get bigger, I'm going to go\nplaces with POKéMON, too.$

replies.text: I hope the first big trip is full of wonderful discoveries and only a manageable number of wet socks.
Curiosity is a good start. I hope someone helps them learn how to look after a partner before the journey begins.
I hope they get a kind partner and somebody they can come home to.
It is lovely to hear somebody imagine a future with so much room in it.
I hope their first packed lunch has something from home in it. Big journeys can begin gently.
They already have the opening line of an adventure. There is plenty of time to discover the rest.
I remember wanting the world to be bigger than the roads I knew. I hope it is kind when they go looking.
I hope they get to learn useful things before they have to improvise them far from home.
Wanting to see somewhere new with a friend beside you is a good dream to keep.
I hope they find their own way of traveling. Looking like the people who inspired you is only the beginning.
I wonder which place they picture first when they talk about going somewhere.

contexts.subject: A prospective student wonders whether school will make rare Pokemon easier to catch.

RustboroCity_Text_CatchRarePokemonIfIGoT.text: POKéMON TRAINER'S SCHOOL!\pIf I go to this school, will I be able\nto catch rare POKéMON easily?$

replies.text: I hope the rare Pokemon have agreed to attend the practical lesson. Otherwise this could become a very long field trip.
School can help with preparation and technique. Finding something rare still involves looking carefully and being patient.
Learning is worth doing even before it gives you the thing you wanted most.
A good lesson might make an ordinary encounter feel more interesting, too. I hope they get that part.
I would like the school to teach care alongside catching. Rare Pokemon still need ordinary meals and kindness.
They have already chosen the most exciting part of the prospectus. The school will now have to explain the homework.
I hope they stay curious when the answer takes more work than they expected.
Good instruction saves a lot of avoidable mistakes. I am a late but enthusiastic supporter of this principle.
I hope they learn to notice the Pokemon they meet, even when those Pokemon are not difficult to find.
There is nothing wrong with having a particular goal. A school may still have more to offer than the quickest route to it.
I would ask the teacher what students actually practice. It would make the hope a little more concrete.

contexts.subject: A resident explains that some Pokemon change appearance as they gain battle experience.

RustboroCity_Text_PokemonCanChangeLookFr.text: If a POKéMON gains experience in\nbattles, it can sometimes change in\lthe way it looks.$

replies.text: A few battles and somebody can become a completely different shape. My own training has mainly changed the shape of my shoes.
Some species evolve as they gain experience. I would be interested in how the trainer notices the approach of that change.
We should pay attention to how a partner feels about changing, as well as how strong it might become.
It must be a strange thing to wake up to a voice that comes out a little differently.
I hope a Pokemon gets the same affection before and after it changes. Growth should not feel like earning permission to be loved.
The cast member may return in an entirely new costume, with no time allowed for alterations. Pokemon have demanding transitions.
I would want someone familiar beside me for a change that large.
I would love to understand how all those parts reorganize. I will begin by keeping an observation notebook, not by poking anyone.
A new shape is still someone we already know. We should leave room for both the difference and the familiarity.
I wonder which familiar habits stay exactly the same afterward. That would make the new appearance feel less strange.
I would like a record of the little things around an evolution, not just the bright moment itself.

contexts.subject: A resident is astonished at the idea of Pokemon changing shape.

RustboroCity_Text_PokemonChangeShape.text: A POKéMON changes shape?\nIf one did that, I would be shocked!$

replies.text: I hope somebody is sitting beside him when he first sees an evolution. That seems like a useful precaution.
It is a reasonable thing to be astonished by, even when it has become familiar to the rest of us.
He is hearing something new. We can let him be surprised without making him feel foolish.
I like hearing the wonder come back into a thing we have started taking for granted.
I hope his first experience of it is a happy one for the Pokemon, too.
He has reached the part of the explanation where the imagination needs a chair. I rather like his honesty.
He has allowed himself to say that it sounds extraordinary. It does, when you stop and think about it.
I would be happy to answer questions. I would also completely understand if the first question were just how.
A familiar fact can still be remarkable. He has reminded us of that.
Somebody should let him finish being amazed before giving him three more facts to absorb.
I would like to see his face when he encounters it for himself. Some discoveries deserve that much attention.

contexts.subject: A resident explains faster growth and possible disobedience for traded Pokemon without enough badges.

RustboroCity_Text_TradePokemonGrowFast.text: A POKéMON you get in a trade from\nsomeone grows fast.\pBut if you don't have certain GYM\nBADGES, it may not obey you…$

replies.text: Growing quickly and listening carefully are apparently separate qualifications. I have known a few people like that too.
Growth does not automatically produce trust or readiness. We should prepare for the partner we are receiving, not just the level it might reach.
I would rather understand what the Pokemon needs than rely on it being impressed by a badge.
It is a lot to ask of a partner: a new home, a new trainer, and instructions from someone it just met.
We should make the new Pokemon feel secure before expecting everything to work smoothly.
A remarkable growth rate and a strongly independent opinion of the director. That could make rehearsal interesting.
Being new somewhere can make even simple instructions feel more difficult. I hope trainers remember that.
Fast growth sounds useful until it outruns your ability to look after it. Planning matters here.
A badge can mark experience. It should not replace the patience involved in getting to know a new partner.
I would rather have a team that is comfortable with us than one that only looks impressive on paper.
I would ask the previous trainer about the Pokemon's habits. Some useful things will never fit on a badge.

contexts.subject: A resident explains that two trainers can jointly challenge a lone trainer with at least two Pokemon.

RustboroCity_Text_YouCanHave2On2Battle.text:
Did you know this?\pYou can have a 2-on-2 battle even
if you're not with another TRAINER.\pIf you catch the eyes of two TRAINERS
when you have two or more POKéMON,\lthey'll both challenge you.\pDon't you think it'd be cool if you
could beat two TRAINERS by yourself?$

replies.text: Two trainers can challenge us at once. I would like a sign I can carry saying ONE CONVERSATION AT A TIME.
Two opponents change the number of interactions we must account for. We should think about how our partners support each other.
Taking on two people is less impressive if we have not prepared our team for it. We can choose our battles.
It sounds like trying to follow two parts at once. You need to hear what they are doing together.
I hope the person walking into that challenge knows they are allowed to get everyone healed first.
Two challengers, one trainer, and no indication that the invitation was carefully scheduled. A busy scene.
I think I would like a little warning before an ordinary walk becomes a coordinated argument with Pokemon.
Now that is a situation where two individual plans can turn into a third, much messier plan. I would prepare for that.
Having two partners beside us should mean giving both of them the attention they need.
I would like to know whether the two opponents have practiced together. Matching enthusiasm does not necessarily make a team.
I would watch the cooperation as closely as the individual moves. That is where the interesting part will be.

contexts.subject: A Devon employee notices a new face and asks whether we transferred to the Trainer School.

RustboroCity_Text_YoureNewAroundHere.text: Oh? Who might you be?\nYou're a new face around these parts.\pHave you just transferred into the\nPOKéMON TRAINER'S SCHOOL?$

replies.text: Our school transfer has been inferred from standing near a school. I hope nobody has already assigned us a desk.
He noticed somebody unfamiliar and offered a plausible place to begin the conversation. We can introduce ourselves.
We are a new face here. It is nice to be asked who we are before someone decides what we need.
I always need a moment to remember how to introduce myself when someone asks unexpectedly.
He is making room for a newcomer in his picture of the town. We can answer kindly.
A new arrival has entered the scene and is immediately offered an educational backstory. Very efficient exposition.
I like being new somewhere better when people sound curious instead of suspicious.
We should ask what the school teaches. Being mistaken for a student is a perfectly good excuse to learn something.
Every familiar person in a town was a new face once. He seems to remember that.
I hope the school is as welcoming to its actual new students as he sounds.
I like hearing how people place a newcomer in their town. It tells us something about the life already here.

contexts.subject: A resident remembers a suspicious person going around the corner.

RustboroCity_Text_SneakyLookingManWentAr.text: Hm? A sneaky-looking man?\pCome to think of it, yes, a shady-\nlooking guy went around the corner.$

replies.text: Around the corner is considerably more useful than somewhere over there. We are making progress toward actual directions.
He has a particular sighting, rather than a general impression. We should keep the route clear in our notes.
We can check the corner without treating everyone we meet beyond it as the same person.
He remembered a small moment that suddenly matters. I hope it helps somebody.
We should thank him for stopping to think. People can notice useful things without realizing it at the time.
The witness has supplied a direction. I shall resist demanding an atmospheric description of the corner as well.
A corner is at least something we can actually go and look at.
We should follow the information we have before inventing a complicated explanation for where he went.
A specific observation is worth treating carefully. We should not let our guesses take its place.
I hope we can come back with news that makes the interruption to his day feel worthwhile.
I would ask which corner before setting off. It is an important detail in a town that has rather a lot of them.

contexts.subject: A resident says Mauville's four-way roads bring people from many places.

MauvilleCity_Text_AllSortsOfPeopleComeTh.text: The roads of this town stretch north\nand south, and east and west.\pBecause of that, we get all sorts of\npeople coming through.$

replies.text: Four directions to arrive from and plenty of people to ask for directions. Mauville seems prepared for my usual navigation method.
A crossroads collects people who might never otherwise meet. I would like to hear what has traveled here with them.
It sounds like a good place to find someone who knows the road ahead.
You could sit here and hear the day arrive in several different accents.
I wonder what everybody is carrying for lunch. A crossroads must have excellent ideas passing through it.
A town where new characters can enter from every side. I imagine the local gossip requires careful filing.
I like places where people can be passing through without having to explain why they are there.
Four routes mean a lot of wear on the roads and a lot of interesting repairs. I would get distracted here.
People can share a place briefly and still leave something with one another.
I would enjoy seeing how people from different places dress for the same journey.
I could spend a whole afternoon here listening to where people have come from. The crossroads would do most of the arranging.

contexts.subject: A resident reminds trainers to heal Pokemon hurt in battle.

MauvilleCity_Text_NurseHurtMonBackToHeal.text: You know, it's cool to have POKéMON\nbattles and stuff…\pBut if your POKéMON gets hurt,\nyou have to nurse it back to health.$

replies.text: That is the part of winning I would hate to forget. Nobody should have to limp through the celebration.
A battle result is only one thing to check afterward. We should pay attention to how every partner is recovering.
Our team trusts us to notice when it hurts. That responsibility does not end when the other trainer loses.
The quiet after a battle is a good time to listen for who is not quite all right.
Yes. Healing, food, water, and a little patience. They should get care without having to ask perfectly.
The dramatic finish should be followed by somebody checking that the whole cast is comfortable.
I like that someone here thought to say it plainly. Care should be part of the routine.
We should fix the damage before setting off to collect any more of it.
A partner is still our responsibility after the exciting part has ended.
I would rather spend extra time getting everyone comfortable than hurry along looking like we have had a productive day.
I want to remember the Pokemon looking well afterward, too. That matters as much as the moment of the win.

contexts.subject: A resident warns that riding a bike does not prevent wild Pokemon encounters.

MauvilleCity_Text_PokemonCanJumpYouOnBik.text: Even if you're riding a BIKE,\nwild POKéMON could jump you.$

replies.text: The Pokemon have not agreed to respect bicycle traffic. I hope somebody has at least explained the bell.
The bike changes how we travel, not whether Pokemon occupy the route. We still need to pay attention.
We should keep the team ready and our eyes ahead. Moving faster is not the same as being out of trouble.
I would prefer to meet a wild Pokemon after I have stopped trying to balance.
We should leave enough room to stop. Startling a Pokemon and falling off a bike sounds unpleasant for everyone involved.
A bicycle does not exempt us from the local cast of surprise encounters. I appreciate the advance notice.
I would like both feet on the ground before negotiating a sudden meeting in the grass.
Good brakes belong on the preparation list. So does remembering that the grass is somebody else's home.
We can move through a place quickly and still owe its inhabitants a little care.
I would rather arrive a little slower than introduce my outfit to the road.
I would watch the path as carefully as the distance we are making. A fast trip still has things in front of it.

contexts.subject: A resident recommends Rydel's Cycles because its owner is generous.

MauvilleCity_Text_RydelVeryGenerous.text: Have you been to RYDEL'S CYCLES yet?\pRYDEL, the owner, is a very generous\nman.$

replies.text: A generous bicycle shop owner sounds like somebody we should meet before my feet write a formal complaint.
I would like to hear what he has done to earn that reputation. People tend to remember practical kindness.
It is good to hear somebody recommend a person, rather than just a price.
I like a town where somebody else's kindness turns into advice given to a newcomer.
I hope he knows people talk about him that fondly when he is not in the room.
The bicycle merchant has received excellent word of mouth before making an entrance. A promising introduction.
It is nice to be directed toward someone because they might make the day easier.
I would enjoy looking at his bikes. I will try not to interpret generosity as permission to rearrange the workshop.
A useful gift can change how much of the world someone gets to see. I would like to meet him.
A good reputation is a lovely thing for a shop to have that cannot simply be painted over the door.
We should ask him how the shop began. I would like to know the person behind the recommendation.

contexts.subject: An enthusiast likes new TV shows, recognizes friends on screen, and hopes to appear on TV too.

MauvilleCity_Text_ExplainTV.text:
Hi, do you check out TV at all?\pThey've added a bunch of cool new
shows recently.\pTV is so cool. I've seen my friends on
TV just out of the blue.\pAnd, sometimes, they even put you on TV
without telling you.\pI wish I would be on TV sometime.\pThat's why I think you should check
out TVs whenever you can.$

replies.text: He would like to appear on television. I would first like to know whether my embarrassing moments have already signed a contract.
Recognizing friends sounds exciting. I am rather more interested in the part about being shown without being told.
I hope people get a choice about being on screen. Being noticed is not always what somebody wanted.
It is strange to imagine your ordinary day turning into a program in somebody else's room.
I hope he gets the sort of appearance he would actually enjoy, with enough warning to tell the people who care about him.
He has declared his availability to an entire medium. I admire the ambition of the audition.
I would like to be asked before becoming somebody's unexpected evening viewing.
The shows sound interesting. I would still prefer advance notice before a camera decides my workbench needs an audience.
A familiar face can make a screen feel friendly. The person on it should get to feel comfortable too.
If I ever appear on television unexpectedly, I would like the courtesy of having dressed on purpose that morning.
I like recognizing people in pictures. I also like asking them whether the picture is one they want shared.

contexts.subject: Wattson gives directions to New Mauville and expresses confidence in us for the generator task.

MauvilleCity_Text_WattsonWontBeChallenge.text:
WATTSON: Don't you worry about it.
It won't be a challenge to you.\pThe entrance to NEW MAUVILLE is just
a short SURF away from ROUTE 110.\pThat's it, then, you have my trust!
Wahahahaha!$

replies.text: He has made the dangerous generator sound like a short errand. I would like us to keep the directions and bring our own caution.
We know where the entrance is. His confidence is encouraging, but it does not replace checking what is unsafe down there.
We can take the job seriously even if he makes it sound easy. Nobody needs us to be careless to prove we can do it.
I appreciate being trusted. I would also appreciate knowing which noises mean we should leave immediately.
We should get everyone ready before going underground. Confidence is easier to carry when the team is comfortable.
A malfunctioning underground generator has received a wonderfully cheerful introduction. I am adding a more cautious stage direction.
I am willing to help. I am also allowed to be a little concerned about the word generator.
I want the power off safely. I do not want to become the interesting sound somebody hears from the next room.
Being trusted with something is a reason to prepare carefully, rather than a reason to stop being afraid of it.
I would like our return to be as reassuring as his send-off. Let us take the practical preparations seriously.
I will remember the entrance route clearly. An unfamiliar underground place deserves a good plan for getting back out.

contexts.subject: After the generator task and reward, Wattson praises younger people taking responsibility.

MauvilleCity_Text_WattsonYoungTakeCharge.text: WATTSON: Wahahahaha!\pIt pleases me to no end to see\nthe young step up and take charge!$

replies.text: He is pleased with us. I am pleased we get to discuss the generator from somewhere above it.
It is good to have the work recognized. I hope the safer system stays that way after we leave.
We handled something that needed doing. We can accept the praise without volunteering for the next emergency immediately.
I like hearing that laugh when the difficult part is over. It sounds rather less like a challenge now.
I hope the next part of taking charge is making sure everyone gets a good rest.
A successful return and enthusiastic applause from the person who sent us. I prefer this arrangement to a dramatic rescue.
We did something useful and got to come back. That is a good ending to hold on to for a moment.
I am glad he is happy. I am also glad we can now call that equipment a completed job.
He put trust in us, and we brought care back to the task. It is nice when those meet properly.
We may enjoy that compliment for a little while before finding something else that needs our attention.
I would like the story to include the preparation as well as the brave part. That is what made the return possible.

contexts.subject: A resident says the winds keep volcanic ash away and praises the clean air for people needing rest.

VerdanturfTown_Text_AirCleanHere.text: The way the winds blow, volcanic ash\nis never blown in this direction.\pThe air is clean and delicious here.\nLiving here should do wonders for even\lfrail and sickly people.$

replies.text: Delicious air. I like that this town has given me a local specialty I cannot accidentally drop.
The wind keeping ash away is useful to know. I would still be careful about promising that a pleasant place can cure everything.
I hope people who come here to recover get the time and support they need, as well as the fresh air.
It does feel easier to take a quiet breath here. I would like to stay still long enough to notice that.
Clean air and somewhere gentle to rest sound like a good beginning for someone who has had a hard time.
The town has successfully marketed a breeze. For once, I think I understand the enthusiasm.
I like that people describe living here as something that can feel good. Not every place has to be exciting.
Knowing which way the ash travels matters. I hope the houses have good ventilation as well as a favorable wind.
A peaceful place can give someone room to recover at their own pace. I hope the people here make that room.
I would enjoy spending an afternoon somewhere that takes being comfortable seriously.
I would like to record how this place feels as well as how it looks. The quiet is part of why people come.

contexts.subject: A child explains that machinery frightened the tunnel's timid Pokemon and a lone man continues digging.

VerdanturfTown_Text_ManTryingToDigTunnel.text:
My papa told me.\pHe says this tunnel is full of
timid POKéMON.\pThey get all scared of loud noise and
make a big uproar.\pSo they had to stop the big tunnel
project.\pBut there's one man. He's trying to dig
the tunnel by himself!$

replies.text: He is digging by himself because the Pokemon could not stand the noise. That is a lot of work to do thoughtfully.
The project had a real effect on the Pokemon living there. I am glad somebody noticed before simply using louder equipment.
I hope he has help and time to rest. Caring about the Pokemon should not mean he has to carry every part of the job alone.
A loud tunnel is somebody else's whole home. It is easy to forget that when you are only passing through.
I would like someone to bring the man a meal while he works. Quiet determination still gets hungry.
An entire construction project stopped for frightened Pokemon, and one man kept looking for a gentler way. That is a story worth hearing.
I understand wanting a route open. I also understand the creatures who cannot simply move away from the noise.
A quieter method may be slower, but the animals living around the work are part of the engineering problem.
He is trying to make room for people without taking all the room away from the Pokemon already there.
I hope the people who eventually use the tunnel know why the work took care and time.
I would like to record the work while it is happening. A finished tunnel might hide how carefully someone tried to make it.

contexts.subject: A child has heard that a man dug the tunnel to reach the woman he loves.

VerdanturfTown_Text_ManDugTunnelForLove.text: There was a man who dug a tunnel for\na lady he loved.\pI don't really get it, but hey!$

replies.text: He wanted to see someone and moved a great deal of rock about it. I hope she appreciated the visit.
Wanting to reach someone can be a powerful reason to keep working. I hope the tunnel is remembered as a shared achievement too.
He found a way to get closer to someone he cares about. That is easier to understand than the amount of digging involved.
It is a love story you can walk through. I rather like that it has ended up useful to other people too.
I hope they get some peaceful time together after all that work. A grand effort should still leave room for an ordinary evening.
A romantic gesture with a measurable reduction in travel time. I am impressed by its range of benefits.
Someone cared enough to make the distance smaller. I think I understand that part.
I admire a romantic gesture that also becomes a useful piece of public infrastructure.
He made a path toward someone he loved, and other people can share it. That is a lovely thing to leave in a place.
I hope the relationship receives as much care as the dramatic part of the story. The visits afterward matter too.
I would like to photograph both ends of the tunnel. It is a connection, and the story belongs on both sides.

contexts.subject: A boy hopes the man breaking the cave's boulders can make a route to Rustboro.

VerdanturfTown_Text_GuyTryingToBustThrou.text:
Did you see the cave next to the
POKéMON MART?\pThere's a guy in there who's trying to
bust up boulders so he can bust out\lthrough to the other side.\pIt'd be great if we could go through…
It'll make it easy to visit RUSTBORO.$

replies.text: He sees a pile of boulders and imagines a convenient trip to Rustboro. That is a very optimistic approach to a rock.
A route through would change how people here travel. I hope the work is planned around the Pokemon in the cave as well.
It would help a lot of people. I hope the person doing the work knows that, and gets some help in return.
It is interesting how a blocked passage can sit in the middle of several people's plans for their day.
An easier way to visit people and get supplies would mean a great deal to the town.
The boy has already planned the sequel in Rustboro. First, somebody needs to finish the rather substantial opening obstacle.
I would like that path to open gently. The people waiting and the Pokemon living there both have reasons to care about it.
I want to see what is actually blocking it. A good solution starts with more detail than a general dislike of boulders.
A little distance on a map can be a very large distance in someone's ordinary life.
I can see why he is eager. Convenient travel changes what you can do without turning a whole day into an expedition.
I would ask him what he would go to Rustboro for first. That would tell us what the tunnel means to him.

contexts.subject: With the tunnel open, a resident is pleased that Devon shopping in Rustboro is easier.

VerdanturfTown_Text_EasyToGetToRustboroN.text: That cave next to the POKéMON MART\nis now a tunnel to the other side.\pIt's great--it's easy to go shop for\nnew DEVON products in RUSTBORO now.$

replies.text: The tunnel is open, and his first great expedition is shopping. I respect a journey with a clearly defined bag at the end.
The benefit is already part of somebody's routine. That is a useful way to measure whether a route matters.
It is good when a difficult piece of work makes ordinary days easier for people.
The route has become familiar enough to be part of a shopping plan. I like hearing what happens after the grand opening.
I hope it also makes visits to friends easier. Groceries are important, but they should not get all the new route to themselves.
A tunnel built with considerable feeling has begun its second career in retail convenience. Places can contain more than one story.
Somebody worked hard, and now he can think about a simple trip instead of a difficult journey. That is a good change.
I would like the builders to hear that. It is satisfying when a finished job starts being useful without needing an explanation.
A path between towns can make both places feel a little less far away from one another.
I hope he enjoys the shopping and gets home without finding that he bought more than he can comfortably carry.
I would like to see what kinds of trips people start making now. The tunnel will keep changing the town in little ways.

contexts.subject: A trainer plans a Battle Tent debut after a winning streak with their Pokemon.

VerdanturfTown_Text_MakeBattleTentDebut.text: My POKéMON and I, we've been riding\na hot winning streak.\pSo I decided to make my BATTLE TENT\ndebut in this town.$

replies.text: A winning streak and a new venue. I hope they have packed the confidence somewhere it cannot squash the sensible preparations.
A different battle format may ask different things of the team. Recent wins are encouraging, but preparation should fit the place.
I hope they can enjoy the challenge without feeling that one loss would erase everything they have done.
A first appearance somewhere new can make even familiar skills feel different. I hope they get a kind start.
I hope the Pokemon get a rest before their debut. A streak can make people forget how much work each win took.
A debut with momentum behind it. I am pleased for them, though I would still rehearse the entrance.
I hope the new experience matters more to them than keeping the record perfect.
Trying a new format is a good way to discover which parts of a plan are actually doing the work.
They have something to feel proud of and somewhere new to grow. I hope both feelings get room.
I hope they remember their first appearance fondly even if the streak ends there. A debut can offer more than a number.
I would like to hear what feels different about this place after their first battle here.

contexts.subject: A resident is worried about suspicious visitors around Professor Cozmo's home.

FallarborTown_Text_ShadyCharactersCozmos.text: Something's happening,\nand I don't like it!\pI've seen shady characters wandering\nin and out of PROF. COZMO's home…$

replies.text: He has noticed something wrong around Cozmo's home. I would rather check on the professor than turn the worry into a rumor contest.
He has seen people arriving and leaving. We should ask what happened without deciding the rest of the account for him.
Somebody should make sure Cozmo is all right. A person's home is a poor place to feel surrounded by strangers.
I dislike hearing that someone has begun to feel uneasy about a familiar doorway.
He sounds genuinely concerned. We can take that seriously without frightening him further with guesses.
The neighbors have noticed an unsettling change in the professor's visitors. That seems worth following up quietly and promptly.
I hope Cozmo has somebody he can ask for help. Being worried about your own home can make it hard to know where to begin.
We should find out what the visitors actually want. There is no useful repair to make from a vague suspicion alone.
A neighbor noticing that something feels wrong can matter a great deal. We should listen carefully.
I would like the professor to have the chance to tell his own part of what is happening.
I would ask when the visitors started coming. A change in routine is sometimes the most useful detail someone has noticed.

contexts.subject: A resident recounts the area's meteor history and the origin story of Meteor Falls.

FallarborTown_Text_RegionKnownForMeteors.text: This region's been known for meteors\nsince the olden days.\pThey say METEOR FALLS was gouged out\nby a falling meteorite long ago.$

replies.text: A falling rock made a landmark people still talk about. I am grateful my dropped belongings have shown less ambition.
The landscape may preserve evidence of that event. I would enjoy comparing the local account with what the rock formations tell us.
It is strange to think an ordinary-looking place can carry the trace of something that sudden and enormous.
People have been telling that story for a long time. I wonder what the first person to hear the impact thought it was.
I hope the area has had quieter days since. It is easier to admire a meteor when it is already part of the ground.
An arrival from the sky with a very enduring effect on the setting. Most dramatic entrances have shorter consequences.
I like places with a history older than anyone who can explain it to us. There is room to wonder there.
I would like to examine what the impact left behind. From a respectful distance, until I know what is stable.
Something that traveled so far has become part of the place people call home. That is an interesting kind of belonging.
The name gives the landscape a story before we have even seen it. I would like to look carefully when we do.
I would try to show the scale in a picture. The interesting part is how much of the old event is still here.

contexts.subject: A girl proudly describes her Azurill as smooth and plushy.

FallarborTown_Text_MyPreciousAzurill.text: See! Take a look!\nThis is my precious AZURILL!\pIt's slick and smooth and plushy, too!$

replies.text: She has delivered a very enthusiastic review of her Pokemon. I hope Azurill is equally pleased with the arrangement.
She clearly notices the small details of a partner she loves. It is nice to hear that kind of attention.
She is proud of Azurill. We can appreciate it without assuming an introduction is permission to pick it up.
She sounds as if every detail is another reason to be fond of it. I like hearing someone talk that way.
I hope Azurill gets as much thoughtful care as enthusiastic praise. They look like happy company for one another.
A complete introduction built around being exceptionally pleasant to hold. Azurill has a very clear public image.
I can see why she wanted to tell someone. Having a little friend can make ordinary details feel worth announcing.
I am keeping my questions about the tail's mechanics to myself for a moment. This is clearly a proud introduction.
She has made it very clear that this Pokemon matters to her. That is the part I would like to remember.
She has described Azurill with excellent attention to texture. I think the little model deserves a break afterward.
I would like a picture of the two of them together. Her expression is as much a part of this introduction as Azurill's.

contexts.subject: The girl's Azurill responds to a greeting.

replies.text: Rooreelooo to you too. That was a much better greeting than anything I had prepared.
It seems happy to answer. We can let a short, comfortable greeting be enough.
Hello, Azurill. We will leave your feet on the ground while we get acquainted.
That little call has a lovely rise to it. I would probably recognize it again after hearing it once.
I hope it gets plenty of quiet time between all the people admiring it. Being adorable can be a busy job.
An extremely brief appearance with considerable charm. I believe the audience is satisfied.
I like the way it answered. There is no need to ask it to do anything else for us.
I am resisting several questions about balance. For now, hello is a perfectly good contribution.
It has greeted us on its own terms. That is a nice beginning.
A delightful little voice. I hope we have not interrupted an important part of enjoying its day.
I would rather let it move naturally than ask it to pose. The little things it chooses to do are interesting enough.

contexts.subject: A resident mentions Flannery's accomplished grandfather and hopes she becomes great in her own right.

FallarborTown_Text_HaveYouChallengedFlan.text:
Have you already challenged FLANNERY,
the LEADER of LAVARIDGE GYM?\pThe girl's grandfather was famous.
He was one of the ELITE FOUR in the\lPOKéMON LEAGUE at one point.\pIt wouldn't surprise me to see FLANNERY
become a great TRAINER in her own\lright.$

replies.text: I hope people ask Flannery about her own battles as often as they mention her grandfather's.
A family history can be interesting without being a complete account of someone's ability. I would like to see her own approach.
She deserves the chance to become good at the job without every step being compared to somebody else.
I know how difficult it can be to hear somebody else's name in the introduction to your own work.
I hope she has people who encourage her when she is learning, not just people waiting to see how she measures up.
A famous predecessor is an impressive introduction and a rather heavy curtain to walk out from behind.
I hope she gets to be herself loudly enough that people learn to begin the conversation with her.
Experience can be passed on. The work of learning what to do with it still belongs to her.
It is kind that he hopes she will succeed. I hope that leaves room for her to succeed in her own way.
A person can inherit a reputation before having any say in it. I would like to hear what she wants to make of hers.
I would like to document her work without making the family comparison the whole caption.

contexts.subject: A child proudly points out the houses built on water and says they were born here.

PacifidlogTown_Text_NeatHousesOnWater.text: See, isn't it neat?\nThese houses are on water!\pI was born here!$

replies.text: He was born in a town that floats. I imagine learning to find your sea legs happens rather early here.
Living above the water must shape a great many ordinary routines. I would like to hear which things he takes for granted.
He is proud of his home. We should let him show us what matters to him about it.
I wonder which sounds tell him he is home before he even looks up.
I would like to know what a family meal feels like with the water moving underneath the house.
He has introduced his hometown and his own beginning in the same breath. A very economical origin story.
Something that feels extraordinary to us has always been home to him. I like remembering that difference.
I want to see how the supports move with the water. I will ask before crawling underneath anything.
A familiar home can be remarkable without needing to feel unusual to the person who grew up in it.
I like the confidence with which he points it out. He knows his home has something worth showing people.
I would ask him which view he likes most. The person who grew up here will notice things a visitor walks straight past.

contexts.subject: A resident warns that the fast current toward Slateport can sweep surfers off course.

PacifidlogTown_Text_FastRunningCurrent.text: The sea between PACIFIDLOG and\nSLATEPORT has a fast-running tide.\pIf you decide to SURF, you could end\nup swept away somewhere else.$

replies.text: The sea has its own travel plans. I would like to read them before contributing us to the itinerary.
We should plan the route around the current rather than assume effort alone will take us where we intended.
We need a way through and a plan for where we could end up. Our partner should not have to solve that alone.
I would like to know the quiet water before learning about the fast water in person.
We should make sure the Pokemon carrying us is ready for that crossing. A warning is a good reason to prepare.
An unexpected destination is entertaining in a story and considerably less charming when your bag is full of seawater.
I prefer surprise changes of plan to happen somewhere I can stand up.
A current is doing work whether we appreciate it or not. We should understand the direction before adding our own effort.
The water does not know where we want to go. We should not mistake it for a path that was laid out for us.
I would rather arrive dry and slightly later than become a cautionary example told by this same person.
I want to look at a map before we set off. A picture of the destination is less useful if we cannot actually reach it.

contexts.subject: A fisherman knows Sky Pillar but prefers sea-level life to climbing it.

PacifidlogTown_Text_SkyPillarTooScary.text:
The SKY PILLAR?\p…Oh, you must mean that tall, tall
tower a little further out.\pIf you asked me, I wouldn't climb it.
It's too scary to get up that high.\pLife at sea level in PACIFIDLOG,
that suits me fine.$

replies.text: He has heard of the very tall tower and chosen the very sensible sea level. I appreciate a clearly stated preference.
Knowing about a place does not oblige him to climb it. We can ask for information without turning it into a dare.
He knows what makes him uncomfortable. I am not going to argue him into a height he does not want.
I can imagine the wind sounding different the farther you climb. I also understand being happy to imagine it from here.
He seems content with the life he has by the water. I am glad he feels able to say so.
He has declined an imposing tower in favor of remaining comfortable. That is a perfectly serviceable character decision.
I would not like to explain my fear of heights to someone who only wanted to talk me out of it.
If we climb it, I want to know the condition of the way up. Height is not the only practical question.
A place can be important without being somewhere everybody needs to go.
I respect a person who can admire a landmark while also having firm plans to remain below it.
A picture from below can still tell us something. We do not need to put him somewhere frightening to hear his view of the place.

contexts.subject: A resident explains that magma heats underground water to supply the springs.

LavaridgeTown_Text_HotSpringsNeverRunDry.text: We draw as much hot water as we need,\nand yet the hot springs never run dry.\pIsn't it magical?\pThese hot springs appear near active\nvolcanoes. Veins of water under the\lground are heated by magma to well up\las hot springs.$

replies.text: The volcano is heating the bathwater. I appreciate it doing something sociable for once.
He has explained the heat source as well as admiring the result. I like his approach.
I can enjoy the warm water while remaining very glad the magma stays underneath it.
All that warmth rising through the ground. It makes sitting still feel connected to something enormous.
Warm water that keeps arriving. I can see why people make a comforting routine of this.
The volcano has accepted a supporting role in a very peaceful afternoon.
I like knowing where the warmth comes from. It makes the quiet here more interesting.
A natural heat supply. I have several engineering questions and a strong desire to sit down first.
Something fierce underground has become a gentle place for people to rest.
I am happy to appreciate the result while keeping a polite distance from the source.
I would like to show the steam against the mountain. They belong in the same picture.

contexts.subject: A girl bathes daily and hopes to become a strong, beautiful Gym Leader like Flannery.

LavaridgeTown_Text_BatheInHotSpringsEver.text: I bathe in the hot springs every day.\pI want to become a beautiful and strong\nGYM LEADER like FLANNERY.$

replies.text: If bathing were the whole qualification, the Gym queue would contain several very wrinkled champions.
Admiring Flannery is a good beginning. I hope she enjoys learning the training part too.
I hope she gets to become someone she likes, rather than an exact copy of somebody else.
I like hearing someone say who has made the future seem exciting to them.
She sounds happy with her routine. I hope her Pokemon enjoy the rest of their day together too.
She has committed admirably to the warmest part of the training program.
I hope she finds out what she brings to the idea herself. That is the interesting part.
The bath might help her relax. Practice will have to take responsibility for the battles.
A role model can show you a possibility without choosing your whole path.
I hope she keeps that confidence when the preparation becomes less comfortable than a bath.
I would like to ask what she admires most about Flannery besides the obvious first impression.

contexts.subject: A bather imagines electric, bubble or lava baths if different Pokemon joined the springs.

LavaridgeTown_Text_IfPokemonInHotSprings.text: If people put POKéMON in hot springs,\nit might be seriously strange.\pWhy, it might be an electric bath, or\na bubble bath, or even a lava bath…$

replies.text: I would prefer to select my bath before the Pokemon accidentally select it for me.
Different Pokemon would need different conditions. The existing bathers would also deserve a say.
We should ask what is safe before inviting the team into somebody else's bath.
I can picture the bubble bath. My imagination is declining the lava option.
Everyone should be comfortable. That includes checking the water rather than assuming warmth suits every Pokemon.
A relaxing bath with an unusually dramatic list of possible special effects.
I would like to keep the surprising part of the bath limited to how relaxed I feel afterward.
An electric bath is an idea I would like to investigate exclusively on paper.
Sharing a space means thinking about what our presence changes for everyone else.
I have already spent enough time choosing my clothes. I am not adding emergency lava-proofing.
I would ask the people who maintain the springs before arranging any aquatic group portraits.

contexts.subject: A bather lists claims that the springs relieve tension, fix romance and attract money.

LavaridgeTown_Text_HotSpringsClaims.text: They're claiming that these hot springs\nare good for calming nervous tension,\lrelieving aching muscles, solving\lromantic problems, and attracting\lmoney…$

replies.text: If the money is attracted to the bath, I would like it to stop hiding in the changing room.
Warm water may be pleasant. The financial and romantic claims could use rather more evidence.
A bath can give us time to think. It is unlikely to do the difficult conversation for us.
I would settle for leaving with my shoulders lower than my ears. The rest sounds ambitious.
Rest is already a good thing to offer. They do not need to promise somebody a whole new life.
Relaxation, romance, and a sudden fortune. The bath has a remarkably demanding contract.
I would be suspicious of water that claimed to understand my romantic problems better than I do.
If it attracts money, I should be able to fund repairs by soaking my invoices.
A little calm might help someone choose what to do next. It does not make the choice disappear.
If wealth arrives, I hope it has the courtesy to wait until I am dressed.
I would ask what people actually enjoy about the springs. That sounds more interesting than the advertisement.

contexts.subject: A bather is surprised that someone our age enjoys hot springs.

LavaridgeTown_Text_OhYouLikeHotSprings.text: Oh, you like hot springs, do you?\pThat's surprising for one as young\nas you.$

replies.text: Apparently enjoying warm water has an age requirement. I hope nobody asks for a membership card.
People can enjoy the same comfort at different ages. It is a useful thing to have in common.
I do not think liking a good rest needs much of an explanation.
Sometimes a quiet afternoon is appealing before anybody thinks it ought to be.
A comfortable bath can be a lovely part of a day at any age.
Our appreciation of warm water has become a surprising character revelation.
I intend to enjoy being comfortable before I receive official permission to look tired.
I have carried tools up enough stairs to appreciate this without waiting any longer.
It is nice when people discover a small pleasure they can share with someone unexpected.
I would rather be surprising in a bath than predictable and aching elsewhere.
I like the idea that this place brings together people who might otherwise never sit and talk.

contexts.subject: The woman accepts our decision not to take the Egg and offers to wait.

LavaridgeTown_Text_AsYouWishThen.text: As you wish, then…\pIf you have a change of heart about\nhatching this EGG, I will be here.$

replies.text: She is willing to wait. I am glad the Egg's future does not depend on us answering quickly.
Taking responsibility for an Egg deserves a considered decision. She seems to understand that.
We should take it when we are ready to care for it properly, not because saying no feels awkward.
It is easier to make a kind decision when someone leaves room to think.
She wants it looked after. Being honest about our readiness is part of doing that.
A very small future has been offered a patient pause. I approve of the pacing.
I like that we can come back after thinking about it.
We can prepare before accepting a responsibility that will eventually hatch.
Waiting can be a thoughtful choice when another life is involved.
She has made the offer without making us feel trapped by it.
I hope she finds the right person, whether that turns out to be us or someone else.

contexts.subject: The Egg cannot be accepted because the traveling party is full.

LavaridgeTown_Text_NoRoomForThisEgg.text: Oh? You've too many POKéMON.\nThere's no room for this EGG…$

replies.text: No room for the Egg. I am glad we checked before attempting creative stacking.
We need an open party space before accepting it. This is a logistical problem with a clear solution.
We can make room carefully and come back. There is no need to rush the team around.
I would rather find out here than halfway down the road with nowhere comfortable to put it.
Let us make sure everyone has a proper place before bringing someone new along.
The arrival has been delayed by a full traveling company. Even an Egg needs a place in the cast.
It is all right to get ready first. The woman is not going anywhere immediately.
This is a capacity limit we should respect without attempting an ingenious workaround.
Making space for someone can take a little thought. We have time to do that kindly.
A safe place for the Egg matters more than pretending our bag is endlessly accommodating.
We know what needs sorting out. Let us do that and return without making a fuss.

contexts.subject: The woman mentions rumors of Eggs appearing at the Pokemon Day Care.

LavaridgeTown_Text_EverySoOftenEggFoundA.text: Every so often, an EGG will be found at\nthe POKéMON DAY CARE.\pOr at least that's how the rumor goes.$

replies.text: The Day Care apparently has occasional surprise residents. I hope its lost-property system is very gentle.
She is careful to call it a rumor. I would ask the people who work there what they have observed.
An Egg appearing means somebody will need to care for it. That part matters whichever account is right.
I wonder how the staff react when they discover a new little possibility in the middle of a normal day.
I hope every Egg they find has someone ready to keep it safe.
A rumor with a small, warm, and potentially very time-consuming conclusion.
I am more interested in who looks after the Egg than in people making the discovery sound mysterious.
The Day Care staff would be better people to ask than a chain of guesses.
However it arrives, it deserves a thoughtful welcome.
I hope the staff get asked about their work as often as they get asked about that rumor.
I would like to hear an actual account from somebody who found one.

contexts.subject: We accept the Egg; the woman hopes we will carry it on plenty of walks.

LavaridgeTown_Text_HopeYoullWalkPlentyWi.text: Good! I hope you'll walk plenty with\nthis here EGG!$

replies.text: We have acquired a very small walking companion with absolutely no opinion about the route yet.
We should keep it safe and include it in our routine. Patient observation is a good beginning.
We have time to give it a gentle start. Let us look after it properly.
I wonder what sounds it will learn to recognize while we are carrying it.
I am already thinking about a comfortable place to rest when we stop for meals.
The company has gained a new arrival before we have even learned its entrance cue.
There is someone new coming with us. That is a nice reason for a walk.
I will keep the tools away from the Egg. This is an important improvement to our packing plan.
We can make a welcoming little place in the journey for it.
It should have a safe spot before we think about making that spot look charming.
I would like to record some of these days, not just the moment it hatches.

contexts.subject: An old man relaxing in hot sand is suddenly nipped by a Pokemon.

LavaridgeTown_Text_PokemonNippedBackside.text: Being buried in this hot sand is…\nSigh…\pSo warm and heavenly…\pEh? Gyaah! Ouch!\pA POKéMON nipped my backside!$

replies.text: The sand treatment has acquired teeth. I would request a very specific explanation before booking it.
That changed the experience abruptly. We should check whether he is hurt and what disturbed the Pokemon.
Let us make sure he is all right before anyone starts laughing about it.
He sounded so peaceful a moment ago. That was a remarkably abrupt ending to the relaxation.
I hope it was only a fright. He should be able to rest without another surprise nip.
A tranquil monologue interrupted by a very committed supporting performer.
I have reconsidered my position on burying the parts of me I cannot easily inspect.
I would like a better survey of the sand before becoming part of the terrain.
We may have found somebody else's occupied patch of sand. I hope everyone can be comfortable again.
I was considering that treatment. The latest testimonial has introduced a concern.
I would put the camera down and see whether he needs help first.

contexts.subject: A sailor loves the sea but feels relieved to reach land after a long voyage.

MossdeepCity_Text_FeelReliefOnLand.text: I'm a SAILOR, so the sea's obviously\nmore important to me.\pBut you know? When I get back on land\nafter a long voyage, I do feel relief!$

replies.text: You can love the sea and still be pleased when the floor stops arguing with your knees.
A familiar profession can still be tiring. His relief makes perfect sense.
Loving the journey does not mean you have to dislike coming home.
I imagine the first quiet night on a floor that stays still feels wonderful.
A proper meal at a table that stays level sounds like a very good welcome.
The sailor has returned to an audience considerably less likely to move underneath him.
I like hearing someone admit that their favorite thing can also wear them out.
Stable ground is an excellent place to put down both your tools and your exhaustion.
A safe return is part of what makes a journey worth loving.
He can be fond of the sea without needing to prove it every waking moment.
I would like a picture of the moment someone spots home from the boat.

contexts.subject: A resident reflects on the connection between sea, living things and the land.

MossdeepCity_Text_LifeNeedsSeaToLive.text:
All life needs the sea to live, even
though it makes its home on the land.\pLife, having run its course, becomes
soil and returns to the land.\pAnd the sea is always connected to
the land.\pYes, like the very shoreline here.$

replies.text: He has given this shoreline a much larger job description than I expected.
The connections matter. The boundary we can see is only one part of a much longer exchange.
It is worth thinking about what happens beyond the edge of the place we are standing.
I like the idea that a shoreline is somewhere things keep meeting, rather than simply ending.
It makes looking after one little place feel connected to looking after a great deal more.
A quiet view with an enormous amount of history arriving at its feet.
I could stand here with that thought for a while.
I want to know how the smaller processes work. Big ideas become more interesting when you can follow the parts.
He is paying attention to a relationship people walk past every day.
I like a view that gives you something to think about after you leave it.
The waterline would make a good place to begin the picture, rather than the place to stop it.

contexts.subject: A sailor reports Magma trouble at Mossdeep and directs us toward the Space Center.

MossdeepCity_Text_MossdeepTargetedByMagm.text:
I heard from a SAILOR buddy that
TEAM AQUA set up shop in LILYCOVE.\pI also heard that someone came along
and wiped the floor with them!\pBut MOSSDEEP here's been targeted
by that TEAM MAGMA.\pIf you want to know what they're up to,
go visit the SPACE CENTER.$

replies.text: One team has barely left the conversation before the other arrives. These uniforms are becoming a terrible travel guide.
The Space Center gives us somewhere to verify the warning. We should learn what is actually happening there.
If people are being threatened, we should find out what help they need.
I would like one of these visits to begin with good news about the people who live here.
We should check on the staff, not just ask what the villains are planning.
The sailor has supplied an address for the trouble. I would prefer that to another ominous hint.
People here deserve better than becoming the next place everyone is worried about.
A Space Center is not somewhere I want Magma experimenting with equipment.
We can take the warning seriously without filling in the unknown parts with panic.
Let us find someone at the center who can tell us what they are facing.
I will keep the sailor's account separate from anything we actually see when we get there.

contexts.subject: A girl wishes the whole world were full of plants and flowers like Mossdeep.

MossdeepCity_Text_NiceIfWorldCoveredByFl.text: Wouldn't it be nice?\pIf the whole world was covered in\nplants and flowers like this island?$

replies.text: A world full of flowers sounds lovely. My nose would like a small seat at the planning meeting.
I like her enthusiasm. Different places and Pokemon would need different kinds of growing things.
She has found something she loves about home and wants other people to have it too.
I would like to hear what all those places sound like when the wind moves through them.
I hope there would be room for vegetable gardens among the flowers. Beauty and dinner can be neighbors.
An ambitious proposal for the world's scenery. I would like to see her first sketch.
I would keep a few quiet paths between the flowers. Somewhere to sit and look at them.
There would be a lot to look after. I hope the plan includes the people doing the watering.
Wanting more living things around us is a lovely wish to begin with.
I would enjoy seeing how people made different kinds of beauty out of the same wish.
I would like to see the places she would choose to plant first.

contexts.subject: Scott notices warnings concerning the Space Center but says they do not concern him.

MossdeepCity_Text_ScottSomethingWrongWit.text:
SCOTT: {PLAYER}{KUN}, feeling good?
I'm doing great!\pI'd heard MOSSDEEP's GYM LEADER is
pretty strong, so I decided to come\ltake a look-see for myself.\pBut there's something wrong about
this town.\pPeople are going on about a warning
letter and the SPACE CENTER…\pI don't think it concerns me in any
way, though.$

replies.text: He noticed the warning and decided it belonged to somebody else's afternoon. A very portable talent.
He has identified a possible problem. I would rather he followed that observation with a useful question.
It concerns the people living here. That is enough reason to pay attention.
It is a strange thing to hear somebody describe a town's worry and step neatly around it.
I hope someone asks whether the Space Center staff are all right.
He has introduced a serious subplot and declined his own involvement in the same speech.
I wish he sounded as interested in worried people as he does in strong trainers.
Equipment getting threatened at a Space Center concerns me quite a bit, actually.
We do not have to be the person directly threatened to care what happens next.
He has excellent confidence in the boundaries of his responsibilities. I would draw them a little differently.
I would like to hear from the people whose warning he has just summarized.

contexts.subject: A resident says Sootopolis has a new Gym Leader who once mentored Wallace.

MossdeepCity_Text_SootopolisNewGymLeader.text:
Ahh… It feels great letting the waves
wash over my feet…\pSpeaking of the waves, you know that
island city SOOTOPOLIS?\pI think the GYM there had a new
LEADER come in.\pPeople tell me the new LEADER once
mentored WALLACE.$

replies.text: Wallace had a teacher. I like finding out that impressive people also had to ask where to begin.
I would be interested in how teaching Wallace shaped the new leader's own approach.
A good mentor can matter long after the student starts doing things differently.
I wonder which habits Wallace kept and which ones he turned into something of his own.
I hope they are both proud of the work they did together.
A teacher steps back into the spotlight after the student has made a name. There is a good conversation there.
It must be interesting to watch someone you taught become someone other people look up to.
I would like to compare their methods. Teaching someone does not mean building an identical copy.
Knowledge can keep moving between people, even after the formal lessons end.
I would rather hear what the new leader wants to do than only measure them against their former student.
I would like a portrait of them together if they wanted one. Their connection is part of both stories.

contexts.subject: A resident talks about the Space Center's large rockets.

MossdeepCity_Text_SpaceCenterLaunchingRo.text: The island's SPACE CENTER has been\nlaunching huge rockets.$

replies.text: Huge rockets. I would like to be both close enough to see and far enough away to remain pleasantly attached to my shoes.
A launch is the visible part of an enormous amount of careful work. I would like to learn about the preparation.
I hope everybody working there gets to see something they are proud of go safely.
I wonder how long you feel the sound after it has finished being a sound.
I hope the staff get a quiet meal after a launch. That sounds like work that makes you forget lunch entirely.
The island has built a way to make an exit genuinely spectacular.
I would like to see a launch with someone who could explain the quiet moments before it.
I have so many questions about the engines that I may need another notebook.
There is something moving about people working together to send something beyond the place they know.
I would choose a very secure hat before standing anywhere near launch day.
I would love to photograph the people watching, as well as the rocket.

contexts.subject: A resident says a recent letter has caused an uproar at the Space Center.

MossdeepCity_Text_SpaceCenterReceivedLet.text: The island's SPACE CENTER has been\nlaunching huge rockets.\pThere's been some kind of an uproar\nover a letter they received recently.$

replies.text: A letter has managed to disturb a building full of rockets. I would like to know what it said.
We should ask somebody who received it. The commotion alone will not tell us the contents.
The people at the center deserve to have the warning taken seriously.
I hope the staff have somebody helping them decide what to do, rather than just everyone worrying at once.
I would ask whether anybody there needs support while they deal with it.
A letter with a very large effect on the room. I would prefer to read the actual message before predicting the next act.
It is unpleasant when an ordinary delivery changes how safe a place feels.
I want to hear from the staff before assuming which part of the equipment is at risk.
We can bring some calm to a worried place by listening before guessing.
I hope the person who has to answer the letter is not having to deal with everything alone.
I would like to know when it arrived and what changed afterward. Those are useful details to begin with.

contexts.subject: A woman explains the white rock symbolizes wishes for safe launches and says she uses wish tags.

MossdeepCity_Text_SpecialSpaceCenterRock.text:
This rock has a special meaning to
the people at the SPACE CENTER.\pThey put it here as their wish for
their rockets to fly safely.\pWhen you make a wish, what do you use?
Do you wish upon a star?\pI use a wish tag to make it happen.
That's what I do.$

replies.text: A small rock carrying a very large hope. I would like the rockets to appreciate the effort.
The wish does not replace the preparation. It gives people a way to express how much a safe return matters.
I hope the people doing the dangerous work know the town is thinking about them.
I like having something quiet to hold the feeling before all that noise begins.
A safe launch means people getting to breathe again afterward. I can understand wanting a little ritual for it.
The stone has no speaking part and still manages to say something important about the town.
I would rather make a small honest wish than pretend not to care because I cannot control the outcome.
I would check every fitting and still understand somebody wanting to leave a wish tag beside it.
A little ritual can give care somewhere to go while we wait.
I like that the wish is for safety. It tells us what people want most from something so impressive.
I would like to photograph the tags with permission. Each one stands for somebody wanting a person to come home.

contexts.subject: A resident loves crossing the sea with Pokemon using Surf.

MossdeepCity_Text_SurfExhilarating.text: A voyage on a ship is fine.\pBut crossing the sea with POKéMON\nusing SURF…\pNow that's an exhilarating trip!\nWouldn't you agree, youngster?$

replies.text: A trip with the sea right there instead of politely underneath a boat. I can see the appeal and feel the splash already.
It must give a different sense of the water. I hope the rider pays as much attention to their partner as to the view.
It sounds exciting. It is also a lot of trust to place in a Pokemon carrying you.
I like the idea of moving at the water's own level for a while.
I hope the Pokemon gets a proper break after carrying someone so far.
A voyage where the traveling companion is also the vessel. That changes the meaning of looking after the company.
I would like a calm patch of sea to begin with. Exhilaration can meet me there.
I would secure the bag carefully before finding out how exhilarating the first wave is.
Sharing a crossing with a partner sounds lovely when both of you are ready for it.
I would prefer to plan my wet clothes in advance rather than discover them dramatically.
The view would be wonderful. I would make sure looking at it did not take attention away from the Pokemon.

contexts.subject: A local struggles to remember the name of Wailmer watching.

MossdeepCity_Text_WailmerWatching.text: Around MOSSDEEP, you can see wild\nWAILMER.\pIt's called, uh…\nWhat was it now…\pWAI, WAI, WAI…\pWAILMER watching!$

replies.text: Wailmer watching. He has introduced it with enough suspense to make a second Wailmer seem necessary.
I like that spotting wild Pokemon has become something people enjoy without needing to catch them.
We could spend a little time looking. There is no need to turn every sighting into a battle.
I would enjoy sitting quietly until one breaks the surface.
That sounds like a good afternoon, especially if we bring lunch and leave the water undisturbed.
A memorable title, eventually delivered. I am happy to wait just as patiently for the actual Wailmer.
I like a hobby that mostly asks us to be still and notice when something wonderful arrives.
I would like to know how close you can get without disturbing them. That seems like the first useful question.
It is nice to enjoy a wild Pokemon while letting it keep its ordinary day.
I would pick a comfortable place to wait. A magnificent sight is easier to appreciate without a cramp.
I would love to try it. I would rather miss a picture than push a Wailmer away from somewhere it wanted to be.

contexts.subject: After we accept the King's Rock, its owner lets us keep it and asks us not to tell Steven.

MossdeepCity_Text_YouCanKeepIt.text: Why would you want it?\nYou're weird.\pYou can keep it, but keep it a secret\nfrom STEVEN.$

replies.text: We have acquired a mysterious rock and a surprisingly specific request about discussing the rock.
Not knowing its use does not make it worthless. I hope we can put it to good use rather than simply pass the mystery along.
We can thank him without making him feel foolish for not wanting it.
I wonder what Steven hoped he would enjoy about it. Gifts can arrive with different meanings than the giver intended.
I hope it finds a purpose with us. It is nicer to pass something on thoughtfully than leave it forgotten.
A gift, a secret, and a rock with a royal title. I had expected a shorter transaction.
I hope he knows he was allowed not to understand the present. Keeping that a secret sounds tiring.
I am interested in finding out what it does. At least we have a name to begin with.
Something can be useful to another person without its first owner having done anything wrong.
I shall try not to announce our discreet acquisition at a volume audible from Steven's house.
I would remember who gave it to us. Its story does not have to end with somebody feeling embarrassed.

contexts.subject: After we decline the King's Rock, its owner continues wondering what it is for.

MossdeepCity_Text_WhatToDoWithWeirdRock.text: Yeah, you think so, too! What are you\nsupposed to do with some weird rock?$

replies.text: We have agreed that it is a strange rock. The mystery has survived the conversation completely intact.
We could ask someone familiar with unusual stones. Agreeing that it is confusing has not supplied much new information.
He does not have to keep something he does not want. I hope he finds someone who understands it.
I wonder how many interesting things spend years waiting for someone to ask the right person about them.
We can decline the gift kindly. The owner still deserves an answer to his question if we find one.
A scene in which two people inspect a mystery and mutually decide to remain uninformed. Surprisingly believable.
I hope he does not feel silly about asking. People learn things by being allowed not to know them first.
Unknown purpose is an invitation to investigate, although I understand not wanting every investigation in your bag.
He was willing to give it away. Perhaps somebody can offer him understanding in return.
I would like him to find out what it is before deciding the gift was pointless.
I would ask Steven about it if we had the chance. He is part of the account we have actually been given.

contexts.subject: The boy points out Steven's house.

MossdeepCity_Text_StevensHouseOverThere.text: STEVEN's house is right over there!$

replies.text: A useful direction to Steven's house. I appreciate an important person being findable without an expedition.
We know where to ask our questions now. I hope we arrive at a considerate time.
We can knock. Knowing where somebody lives is not permission to surprise them inside it.
I like learning where someone belongs when they are not out doing the things people know them for.
I hope he gets ordinary quiet evenings here too.
The celebrated trainer has a house over there. Fame occasionally has pleasantly practical geography.
It is nice to think of someone impressive getting to close a familiar door behind them.
I would enjoy hearing about his collection. I will ask before inspecting anything in it.
Having a place to come back to matters, however far somebody travels.
I hope visitors remember it is his home before treating it like a destination.
I would ask him what he likes about living on this island. An address is only the beginning of that answer.

contexts.subject: A local dismisses Bug Catchers as hobbyists while praising Brock as a serious trainer.

PewterCity_Text_BrockOnlySeriousTrainerH.text:
There aren't many serious POKéMON
TRAINERS here.\pThey're all like BUG CATCHERS,
you know, just hobbyists.\pBut PEWTER GYM's BROCK isn't like
that, not one bit.$

replies.text: I would like to hear him explain that distinction to a very determined Beedrill.
An interest can begin as a hobby and still involve considerable knowledge and care.
Taking good care of a Wurmple counts. Brock being capable does not make everyone else pointless.
I dislike the idea that enjoying something makes your effort less real.
I hope the Bug Catchers here know somebody appreciates what they do.
He has appointed himself critic of the local training scene. The review seems rather narrow.
I would rather be sincerely interested in something than perform seriousness for somebody like that.
I have learned useful things from people who were supposedly just messing about.
There is room for more than one way to care about Pokemon.
He could praise Brock without dressing everybody else down first.
I would like to hear the hobbyists describe their own work.

contexts.subject: Having led us to the gym, the guide urges us to challenge Brock.

PewterCity_Text_GoTakeOnBrock.text: If you have the right stuff,\ngo take on BROCK!$

replies.text: He has delivered us to the challenge. I hope there is equally enthusiastic guidance toward lunch afterward.
We know where the Gym is. We can still decide when the team is ready.
Being shown the door does not mean we have to walk through it immediately.
He sounds excited for us. I hope the nerves leave some room to enjoy the first step.
We should check that everybody is comfortable before accepting the invitation.
Our entrance has been arranged. I would still like a moment with the script.
I prefer encouragement that leaves room to take a breath first.
We have reached the right building. Preparation remains our responsibility.
We can be grateful for the help and choose our own pace.
I hope he enjoys hearing how it went when we come back out.
I would remember this spot. First arrivals can look ordinary once they become familiar.

contexts.subject: The guide has led us to the museum and says the admission fee is worthwhile.

PewterCity_Text_ThisIsTheMuseum.text: This is it, the MUSEUM.\pYou have to pay to get in, but it's\nworth it. See you around!$

replies.text: A personal escort to some fossils. I had expected the ancient things to be harder to arrange a meeting with.
I would like to see the collection. We can ask what the admission helps the museum look after.
He wanted us to see something he likes. That is a pleasant reason to show a visitor around.
I like an introduction that ends with time to look for ourselves.
I hope we have enough time to enjoy the visit instead of hurrying past the interesting parts.
The guide has made a very committed recommendation. I am ready to meet his chosen supporting cast of fossils.
I like knowing somebody wanted us to find this place.
I would enjoy seeing how the exhibits are preserved. I will keep my hands safely to myself.
Sharing a place you love is a kind way to welcome someone.
I appreciate being told about the fee before arriving at the desk with empty pockets.
I would like to see which exhibit made him so eager to bring people here.

contexts.subject: A museum enthusiast asks whether we found the Mt. Moon fossils amazing.

PewterCity_Text_WerentThoseFossilsAmazin.text: Weren't those fossils from MT. MOON\namazing?$

replies.text: They are excellent at making a little afternoon feel rather short and recent.
A fossil can preserve evidence of a life nobody living has ever seen. Yes, that is remarkable.
It is worth stopping to think about what those shapes used to belong to.
I like imagining the quiet before anyone put a name beneath the glass.
I am glad people have kept them somewhere we can learn from them.
They have remained compelling for an exceptionally long time without improving their presentation.
I like that something so old can still make a person sound this excited.
I have questions about the preservation process. Several pages of questions, unfortunately.
A small piece of a long-gone life can still change how somebody sees the world.
I like seeing a display someone has cared enough to make clear and beautiful.
I would try to capture the scale. Tiny details deserve room in the picture too.

contexts.subject: After we say we understand what he is doing, the gardener emphasizes the effort.

replies.text: He sounds pleased we noticed the work. I hope his garden gives him a peaceful afternoon back.
Routine work can disappear from people's notice until it stops being done.
It is good to acknowledge somebody keeping an ordinary place in order.
I wonder whether he likes the quiet part after he has finished.
I hope somebody brings him a drink when he needs a break.
He has accepted our recognition and added a strongly worded footnote about the labor involved.
Sometimes being seen trying is the thing you wanted from a conversation.
I appreciate maintenance. People tend to notice it most enthusiastically after something fails.
A cared-for place usually has somebody's effort behind it.
I hope he knows the garden is appreciated when nobody happens to mention it.
I would like to see the place before and after a season of his work.

contexts.subject: A resident finds our work on a Pokemon encyclopedia amusing.

CeruleanCity_Text_PokemonEncyclopediaAmu.text: You're making an encyclopedia on\nPOKéMON? That sounds amusing.$

replies.text: An encyclopedia. A respectable name for a very long walk interrupted by wildlife.
I like recording what we learn. It becomes much more useful when somebody else can understand the notes.
It is a big project. We can be proud of learning one thing properly at a time.
I wonder which entry will end up reminding us most clearly of an ordinary day on the road.
I hope the record includes the little things that help people care for their partners.
Our extensive wandering has acquired an academically impressive description.
I would like to leave some room in the notes for things we do not understand yet.
I support useful documentation. This is me attempting to learn from several personal disasters.
Paying attention can become something other people get to share.
I would enjoy making the pages clear enough that the interesting parts are easy to find.
I would like the pictures to show something the written entry cannot quite explain.

contexts.subject: A fellow trainer remarks on the work involved in collecting and battling.
