CeruleanCity_Text_TrainerLifeIsToughIsnt.text: You're a TRAINER, too?\pCollecting, battling…\nIt's a tough life, isn't it?$

replies.text: He has noticed the part between the heroic poses. It contains a surprising number of chores.
It is demanding work when you take the care as seriously as the results.
We do not have to pretend every day is easy to prove we want to be here.
Some days the journey feels longer than the map suggested. I like that he understands.
I hope he has somebody reminding him to eat and rest when the day gets away from him.
Adventure has an extraordinary amount of uncredited preparation.
It helps when somebody says the hard part out loud without turning it into a competition.
Things going smoothly usually means somebody did the dull preparations properly.
We can love the life and still need a little care ourselves.
I appreciate a conversation that allows us to admit we have sore feet.
I would like to hear which parts still make the effort worthwhile for him.

contexts.subject: A girl wants a bright red bicycle but plans to keep it indoors so it stays clean.

CeruleanCity_Text_WantBrightRedBicycle.text: I want a bright red bicycle.\pI'll keep it at home, so it won't\nget dirty.$

replies.text: An indoor bicycle. At least the hills should be manageable.
She can enjoy how it looks. I suspect riding it might give her another reason to like it.
It is hers to enjoy. I hope keeping it perfect does not turn into worrying about it constantly.
I understand liking an object before knowing everything you want to do with it.
I hope she gets some happy days with it, whether they happen indoors or out.
A vehicle cast exclusively as a decorative presence. Bold use of the equipment.
I would want to take it somewhere once the fear of the first scratch wore off.
The moving parts would like a word about their future employment.
Something can be beautiful and still have a life outside the room.
I understand the color choice. I would personally allow the tires a little adventure.
I would like a picture from its first outing, if she ever chooses one.

contexts.subject: After Slowbro ignores commands, its trainer says obedience depends on the trainer's abilities.

CeruleanCity_Text_HardToControlMonsObedi.text: No! That's wrong!\nIt's so hard to control POKéMON!\pYour POKéMON's obedience depends\non your abilities as a TRAINER.$

replies.text: Slowbro has reviewed the instructions and returned them without comment.
Understanding the partner may help more than issuing the next command more firmly.
He is frustrated. I hope that does not become a reason to stop listening to Slowbro.
They do not seem to be hearing the same rhythm yet.
I would give them a quiet moment together instead of adding another person shouting advice.
The director has discovered that having a line ready does not guarantee a performance.
I hope Slowbro gets a chance to communicate something besides apparent refusal.
He has noticed a problem. Repeating the same approach is unlikely to explain it.
A relationship needs room for something other than instructions.
I hope they find a way to work together without making every attempt a public argument.
I would listen to what he has already tried before deciding what the difficulty is.

contexts.subject: A resident explains that Slowbro blocks access to a tree but another way around exists.

CeruleanCity_Text_IfSlowbroWasntThereCou.text:
If that SLOWBRO wasn't there, you
could CUT down the small tree.\pThat way, you could get to the
other side.\pI think there's a way around it,
though.$

replies.text: A Pokemon, a tree, and a possible detour. Navigation has assembled a small committee.
If another route is available, we can check it before making either Slowbro or the tree the problem.
We can go around without treating a resting Pokemon like an obstacle that owes us an apology.
A slightly longer walk sounds nicer than beginning an argument with the scenery.
I am happy to take the detour if everyone gets to stay comfortable.
The shortest route has two very quiet objections standing on it.
I like that he mentioned a way around before we started inventing dramatic solutions.
I would check the alternative first. A route can be inconvenient without needing reconstruction.
Passing through should not always mean making everything else move.
A few more steps are cheaper than a thoroughly unnecessary scene.
I would like to know where the other route begins. That is the useful part for us now.

contexts.subject: A resident explains Cut but also points out a way around the small tree.

CeruleanCity_Text_YouCanCutDownSmallTree.text:
Did you know that you can CUT down
small trees?\pEven that small tree in front of
the shop can be CUT down.\pI think there's a way around it,
though.$

replies.text: We can cut it, or we can walk around. I appreciate the tree receiving a place on the options list.
A technique being available does not mean it is the best answer to every small inconvenience.
If the way around is easy, I would try that before making work for the team.
I would like to see what is along the other path anyway.
We can take a few extra steps. It might give everybody a pleasant little break.
The dramatic application of a technique has been challenged by an ordinary detour.
I like knowing we have another choice before doing something we cannot take back.
I would compare the effort involved before treating every tree as an engineering assignment.
We can find our way through a place without always changing its shape.
I am quite willing to sacrifice the perfectly straight route to a nicer walk.
The route around might show us something the shortcut would have hidden.

contexts.subject: A police officer describes a Rocket burglary and the difficulty of dealing with the gang.

CeruleanCity_Text_PeopleHereWereRobbed.text: The people here were robbed.\pIt's obvious that TEAM ROCKET is\nbehind this most heinous crime!\pEven our POLICE FORCE has\ntrouble with the ROCKETS!$

replies.text: The people inside have already had a terrible day. I hope the attention stays on helping them recover.
We should separate what the officer knows from what still needs investigating. The victims deserve a careful account.
They need their home to feel safe again. That matters beyond catching the person responsible.
It is hard to imagine a familiar room after someone has made it feel like that.
I hope somebody has asked what the residents need right now.
A burglary leaves more behind than a scene for other people to examine.
I hope the people living here have somewhere they can sit without having to answer questions for a while.
There will be damage to put right. I would like the practical help to arrive as promptly as the speculation.
A person's home should belong to them again after the investigation, not to everyone else's curiosity.
I hope they are given privacy as well as sympathy.
I would ask permission before documenting anything here. It is still somebody's home.

contexts.subject: The cave guard explains that exceptionally strong Pokemon require a highly accomplished trainer.

CeruleanCity_Text_ThisIsCeruleanCave.text:
This is CERULEAN CAVE.\pHorribly strong POKéMON live inside
there.\pIt takes a very special TRAINER to
be allowed inside there.\pYou'd have to be strong enough to
become the POKéMON LEAGUE\lCHAMPION for starters.\pAnd, you would have to have
made a great achievement.$

replies.text: The cave has a rather demanding admissions policy. I would prefer to arrive qualified rather than test how literal the warning is.
A place with unusually strong Pokemon deserves preparation, even from someone with an impressive record.
We should go when our team is ready, not simply when a guard stops objecting.
I would like to know the way back as carefully as the way in.
Nobody should have to carry us into a dangerous place just because we are eager to see it.
The entrance has given us unusually clear notice that the next scene may be difficult.
I do not think the warning becomes less serious because we are curious.
I would prepare supplies and a route before presenting our qualifications to the cave itself.
Being allowed somewhere is not quite the same thing as being ready to care for one another there.
I would rather leave an impressive cave for another day than make the team pay for our impatience.
There will be plenty to notice when we are prepared enough to look without panicking.

contexts.subject: A landowner describes plans for a building while his Pokemon levels the ground.

VermilionCity_Text_BuildingOnThisLand.text: I'm putting up a building on this\nplot of land. I own it all.\pMy POKéMON is tamping the land\nto lay the foundation.$

replies.text: He owns the plot. The Pokemon appears to own most of the current workload.
A good foundation matters. I hope the Pokemon doing the work gets appropriate breaks and care.
I would like to hear as much about the worker's needs as the owner's plans.
I wonder what he imagines here once the sound of tamping finally stops.
I hope there is a meal and a proper rest planned for the Pokemon as well as a building.
The owner has announced his future masterpiece. The supporting performer is currently doing the groundwork.
I hope he thanks the Pokemon as confidently as he describes owning the land.
I would enjoy hearing about the foundation design. I would also like to see a reasonable work schedule.
Making a place should involve caring for the one helping you make it.
I hope the finished building leaves some evidence of the work the Pokemon put into it.
I would begin the record before the building exists. The worker belongs in the history too.

contexts.subject: Machop is flattening the ground for the future building.

VermilionCity_Text_MachopStompingLandFla.text: A MACHOP is stomping the land flat.$

replies.text: That is a very determined method of persuading a piece of ground to be flatter.
Machop is doing useful physical work. We should avoid getting in its way or treating it like a demonstration.
I hope it gets regular breaks. Working hard does not mean being ready to work forever.
That steady rhythm must become part of the street after you hear it long enough.
I hope somebody has water ready when it stops.
An impressive performance of a practical task. It deserves more than being called part of the equipment.
I hope it likes some part of the job, rather than only being very good at it.
I would ask how it signals that it needs a break before adding any more work.
A helpful Pokemon is still someone whose comfort matters.
I would like the finished place to remember its first hard worker.
I would ask before taking a picture while it works. A pause might be more welcome than an audience.

contexts.subject: A resident says the luxury S.S. Anne visits Vermilion once each year.

VermilionCity_Text_SSAnneVisitsOnceAYear.text: The S.S. ANNE is a famous luxury\ncruise ship.\pIt visits VERMILION once a year.$

replies.text: One visit a year. I hope the ship makes an effort to remember everybody's birthday while it is here.
An annual visit must become part of how people here mark the seasons.
I wonder who waits for it because someone they know might step off.
A ship returning to a familiar harbor has the beginning of a good song in it.
I would like to know what special food appears in town when the passengers arrive.
A yearly entrance with considerable anticipation. The ship has excellent timing for a recurring role.
I like the idea of a familiar arrival that still gives people something to look forward to.
I would love a look at the maintenance work between those glamorous visits.
A place can have a relationship with something that only stays briefly.
I hope the people who work aboard get to enjoy the visit as well as arrange it for everyone else.
I would like pictures of the harbor before and after it arrives.

contexts.subject: Oak's aide directs us to another aide carrying a package near Route 2.

VermilionCity_Text_Route2AideHasPackageF.text:
Oh, hello, {PLAYER}!
How are you doing?\pIt's me, one of PROF. OAK's AIDES.\pDid you meet the other AIDE?\pHe had a package from PROF. OAK
for you, {PLAYER}.\pHe said he'd look for you around
ROUTE 2, {PLAYER}.\pIf you're in the ROUTE 2 area,
please look for him.$

replies.text: The aides have organized a small relay of people telling us where the package is.
Route 2 gives us a useful place to look. We should introduce ourselves before assuming every aide is expecting us.
We know where to ask now. There is no need to rush the person making the delivery.
I like knowing somebody remembered to help us find what was meant for us.
I hope the other aide has not spent the whole day looking up the wrong road.
A package with a supporting cast and a short geographical subplot.
I hope we manage to find one another before everyone has to make another trip.
A clear destination would have improved the delivery plan, but this is a useful update.
Somebody is making sure a kind intention reaches the person it was meant for.
I would like the next conversation to include the actual package.
I will remember Route 2. It is the part of the message that will help us find him.

contexts.subject: A resident explains that memorial services for Pokemon are held in the tower.

LavenderTown_Text_TownKnownAsMonGraveSit.text: This town is known as the grave\nsite of POKéMON.\pMemorial services are held in\nPOKéMON TOWER.$

replies.text: We should take our time and be considerate here. People have come with someone on their minds.
A place for remembrance gives grief somewhere it can be acknowledged without explanation.
We can be quiet without making a show of it. This is somebody else's difficult day.
I hope the people coming here have someone to sit beside them afterward.
I would like to know whether anyone needs help with the little things that are difficult while grieving.
Some places do not need us to supply anything impressive to say.
Remembering can be painful and still be something you want to do.
I will keep my tools and questions quiet unless somebody asks for help.
The love does not end because the life did. It makes sense to have a place for it.
We should let people choose whether they want company or privacy.
I would keep the camera away unless somebody specifically wanted a memory recorded.

contexts.subject: A resident suspects the tower ghosts are Pokemon killed by Rocket.

LavenderTown_Text_GhostsAppearedInTower.text: Ghosts appeared in POKéMON TOWER.\pI think they're the spirits of\nPOKéMON that the ROCKETS killed.$

replies.text: That is an awful thing to imagine. I would like us to find out what happened without treating it as entertainment.
It is a serious account. We should be careful about what is known, what is feared, and who needs help.
If Rocket hurt Pokemon here, the people grieving deserve more than a rumor passed around the street.
I wish the story began with someone being kind to the Pokemon before any of this happened.
I hope there is someone helping the Pokemon and the people left hurting.
A frightening story can still concern real grief. It should be handled with care.
I do not want someone else's loss turned into a reason for visitors to be excited.
I would rather work out what can be put right than collect a more dramatic version of the story.
If something here cannot rest, I hope somebody will listen to what it needs.
I hope the people affected get to speak for themselves.
I would ask gently and avoid recording anything somebody does not want to revisit.

contexts.subject: After we affirm belief in ghosts, the girl acknowledges that there are other believers.

replies.text: She sounds glad not to be the only person saying it. We can listen without making the conversation a contest.
I am interested in what she experienced. Agreeing to listen is a useful beginning.
She does not have to convince an entire street before somebody treats her kindly.
It can be a relief to hear someone answer without laughing first.
I hope talking about it helps her feel less alone with whatever worried her.
She has found an audience willing to hear the account. We should let it remain her account.
I know the relief of discovering you do not have to explain yourself quite so hard.
I would ask what she noticed before asking for conclusions.
There are ways to make room for someone's experience without demanding that it become a performance.
I hope she feels comfortable enough to say what she means at her own pace.
I would rather hear her actual memory than prompt her into the story I expected.

contexts.subject: A resident recommends the Safari Game for its unusual Pokemon.

FuchsiaCity_Text_DidYouTrySafariGame.text: Did you try the SAFARI GAME?\pThere are some rare POKéMON that\ncan only be caught there.$

replies.text: New Pokemon and a place to wander. I hope the excitement leaves enough attention for the way back.
I would enjoy observing species we have not encountered yet. Their habits interest me as much as their rarity.
We should learn the rules before going in, and be considerate of the Pokemon living there.
I would like to see which sounds become familiar before we find the Pokemon making them.
I hope the visit gives us time to notice how the Pokemon are doing, too.
An excursion promising unusual encounters. I shall try not to treat the ordinary ones as disappointing extras.
I would like a quiet moment to look before everybody starts deciding what to catch.
I would check the equipment and rules first. Excitement is a poor substitute for either.
Being rare does not mean a Pokemon owes a visitor a meeting.
I would enjoy seeing something unfamiliar without immediately trying to make it part of our luggage.
I would love to go looking, provided we let the wildlife choose how close to come.

contexts.subject: A visitor discovers the apparent item ball in the exhibit is actually a Pokemon.

FuchsiaCity_Text_ItemBallInThere.text: That item ball in there…\nWere you wanting that?\pMe, too!\n…Huh? That's a POKéMON?$

replies.text: The tempting item has developed a private life. We should probably stop planning to pocket it.
It is a useful reminder to identify what we are looking at before deciding what we want from it.
Good thing we stopped to look. The Pokemon deserves better than an argument over who found it first.
It has completely changed the conversation without doing anything at all.
I hope it is comfortable while people keep mistaking it for something to collect.
An excellent reveal from a performer who has remained impressively still.
I would prefer to be recognized as a person before somebody decided I was a prize.
That is a fairly consequential identification error. I am glad the correction arrived early.
Noticing that it is alive should change how we approach it.
I admire a Pokemon that can make an entrance by simply continuing to be where it already was.
I would spend a little longer looking now. The interesting part was there before we understood it.

contexts.subject: The Gym Leader's daughter is training to match her father's skill with Poison Pokemon.

FuchsiaCity_Text_MyFatherIsGymLeader.text: My father is the GYM LEADER of\nthis town.\pI'm training to use POISON POKéMON\nas well as my father.$

replies.text: She has a very specific family tradition to live up to. I hope the household labels its lunch containers carefully.
Learning from her father gives her a starting point. Her own methods will be interesting to see.
I hope people notice the work she does, instead of only comparing her with him.
She sounds determined. I wonder what part of his teaching she will eventually make her own.
I hope they get time to enjoy being family as well as being teacher and student.
A successor preparing her own entrance. I would like her to get a little room to surprise the audience.
It can be hard to know where admiration ends and expectations begin. I hope she gets to choose.
I would like to hear how they train safely with those partners. That is part of the skill too.
She can learn from someone she loves without becoming the same person.
I hope she keeps a sense of her own style while learning what she admires in his.
I would like to record her progress before everybody starts treating the outcome as inevitable.

contexts.subject: A resident distinguishes the entrance displays from the Safari Game beyond them.

FuchsiaCity_Text_SafariZoneZooInFront.text: The SAFARI ZONE has a zoo in front\nof the entrance.\pOut back is the SAFARI GAME for\ncatching POKéMON.$

replies.text: A place to look first and a place to explore afterward. I appreciate directions in the order my feet need them.
We should understand the different rules for the displays and the area beyond them.
We can enjoy meeting the Pokemon here without treating them like the ones we might catch farther in.
I would like a slow look around before choosing whether to spend the rest of the day exploring.
I hope both areas have people paying close attention to the Pokemon's comfort.
The introduction and the expedition have helpfully been given separate entrances.
It is nice to know we can simply look around without committing to the whole excursion.
I would ask about the facilities before going beyond the entrance. Useful directions are a good start.
Different ways of sharing a place with Pokemon come with different responsibilities.
I appreciate knowing what sort of visit we are choosing before I have dressed for the wrong one.
I would like to see how people behave around the displays before deciding how to approach the wider area.

contexts.subject: Erik is waiting for Sara at the place they agreed to meet.

FuchsiaCity_Text_WheresSara.text: ERIK: Where's SARA?\nI said I'd meet her here.$

replies.text: The meeting place has been successfully found by half the meeting. I hope the other half arrives soon.
I would check exactly where they agreed to meet before assuming something has gone wrong.
He sounds worried. We should avoid supplying reasons to worry that he has not actually been given.
Waiting makes every approaching footstep seem briefly important.
I hope Sara gets here soon and they can enjoy the visit they planned.
One character has arrived precisely on cue. The scene is waiting patiently for its second line.
I dislike how quickly waiting can turn into guessing what somebody is thinking.
This sounds like a job for confirming the meeting point before devising a complicated search.
We can offer a little calm without pretending to know why she is late.
I hope they both recognize the exact same here when they describe where they meant to meet.
I would ask whether there is another entrance. It is a practical question before a dramatic conclusion.

contexts.subject: A resident says scientists experiment in the burned-out Pokemon Mansion.

CinnabarIsland_Text_ScientistsExperiment.text: Scientists conduct experiments \nin the burned-out building.\pYou know, the one they call the\nPOKéMON MANSION.$

replies.text: A burned-out building is a bold place to continue announcing experiments. I hope the next word is safely.
I would like to know what the work involves and whether the building is fit for it.
People doing research still deserve a safe place to do it.
A place can look abandoned and still contain someone's working day. I hope they are looking after themselves.
I hope the Pokemon there are receiving more care than the building appears to have had.
The setting has already supplied a rather strong warning. I would pay attention to it.
I would like to know what we are walking into before the door closes behind us.
I have worked in questionable rooms. The word burned-out would give me pause.
Knowing a place has been damaged should make us more careful about the lives still inside it.
I would prefer a clearer account of the safety arrangements before admiring the commitment to research.
I would ask permission before approaching anyone's work, and find out which parts are safe to visit.

contexts.subject: A resident calls Blaine unusual and says he lived on Cinnabar before the laboratory existed.

CinnabarIsland_Text_BlaineLivedHereSince.text: CINNABAR GYM's BLAINE is quite the\nodd fellow.\pHe's lived on the island since way\nbefore the LAB was built.$

replies.text: Blaine has been here long enough to have opinions about the island before it acquired laboratory paperwork.
He may remember changes that the newer institutions take for granted. I would enjoy hearing that account.
I would rather meet him than decide what being unusual is supposed to mean.
I wonder which version of the island he thinks of first when he says home.
I hope there are still familiar things he enjoys here after so much has changed.
A long-running local character with an island's worth of backstory. I would let him choose where to begin.
Sometimes people mean unfamiliar to me when they say someone is odd.
I would like to ask what changed when the lab was built. Long-term residents notice practical details.
A person can carry a history of a place that its newest buildings do not show.
He deserves an introduction larger than the local verdict on his personality.
I would like to see any old photographs he wanted to share. His account could give them a different meaning.

contexts.subject: Amy says fighting two trainers requires thinking about many things.

Route103_Text_AmyPostBattle.text: AMY: You have to think about all\nkinds of things when you're battling\lagainst two TRAINERS.$

Route103_Text_AmyRematchPostBattle.text: AMY: You have to think about all\nkinds of things when you're battling\lagainst two TRAINERS.$

replies.text: Two trainers, several Pokemon, and my own internal commentary. A busy afternoon for your attention.
The interactions between the partners matter as much as the individual moves.
We can prepare together instead of expecting one person to notice everything at once.
Following two parts becomes easier once you hear what they are doing together.
It helps to know what each partner needs before the noise begins.
A crowded scene rewards somebody who remembers to look beyond the nearest dramatic gesture.
I appreciate her admitting that there is a lot to keep track of.
Two working plans can produce a third, unexpected problem when they meet.
Cooperation asks us to notice someone else's needs alongside our own.
I would rather have a clear shared plan than two impressive performances getting in each other's way.
I would pay attention to the moments when one partner changes what the other can do.

contexts.subject: Andrew remains angry after the battle.

replies.text: He is still boiling. I would give that kettle a little space.
Another argument is unlikely to help him think clearly about the battle.
We do not have to stand here until he is ready to be pleasant.
I would like the next sound we hear to be somewhere a little quieter.
I hope he takes a break before asking his team to carry that mood into another battle.
The battle has ended, but the dramatic temperature remains impressively high.
He can have his feelings without making us responsible for fixing them.
I would let everything cool before trying to identify what went wrong.
Some space might be kinder to everybody involved.
I hope his Pokemon are getting a gentler reception than the rest of the world.
I would not ask him for a portrait at this particular moment.

contexts.subject: Daisy describes aromatherapy and calming fragrances.

Route103_Text_DaisyPostBattle.text: Aromatherapy is a form of mental\nhealing that works with fragrances.$

replies.text: I like a conversation about smells that does not end with somebody noticing our laundry.
People find different things calming. I would ask which fragrances she particularly enjoys.
It is good to have something quiet you can turn to after a busy day.
A familiar scent can bring a whole room back to mind.
I like the way a kitchen can start feeling welcoming before anybody reaches the table.
A room can establish its mood before anyone says the first line.
I have a few scents I would happily carry a little farther into a difficult day.
I would label everything clearly before beginning any investigation involving fragrant bottles.
A small comforting ritual can make space to breathe.
I would like to know what she chooses for herself when nobody else is there to impress.
That is something a photograph cannot keep by itself. I would write the memory beside it.

contexts.subject: Isabelle apologizes for nearly colliding with us while practicing swimming.

Route103_Text_IsabellePostBattle.text: I'm a poor swimmer so I was practicing…\nSorry for almost crashing into you.$

replies.text: She apologized. I am happy for our next meeting to involve rather less accidental momentum.
Practicing is easier with enough space and appropriate support. I hope she has both.
We are all right. She can keep learning without feeling that one mistake defines the afternoon.
It is nice that she stopped to make sure the awkward moment ended kindly.
I hope she is comfortable and has someone looking out for her while she practices.
An accidental entrance, gracefully acknowledged. We can leave the collision out of the review.
I appreciate the apology. Learning something in public can feel very exposed.
I would rather give her more room than stand close and critique every movement.
A little patience is a useful thing to offer someone who is still learning.
Nobody needs to make the apology more embarrassing than it already feels.
I would rather remember her stopping to check on us than the moment before it.

contexts.subject: Liv is puzzled that she and her big sister lost despite working well together.

Route103_Text_LivPostBattle.text: LIV: We work perfectly together,\nme and my big sister…\pBut we still lost…$

replies.text: A perfect partnership can still encounter a thoroughly inconvenient us.
Coordination is valuable, but a particular matchup may still require a different plan.
Their teamwork was not wasted because they lost. They should keep what worked.
Playing together well does not mean every song ends where you expected.
I hope they are kind to each other while deciding what to try next.
A good cast can have a difficult performance without ceasing to be a good cast.
It is easier to learn from a loss when it does not become a reason to blame the person beside you.
The parts can work together and still need a different overall arrangement.
The trust between them is something they can carry into the next attempt.
I hope they notice the things they did well as clearly as the result they wanted.
I would like to hear them work out the next plan together.

contexts.subject: After another loss, Liv again questions why the sisters' partnership did not win.

Route103_Text_LivRematchPostBattle.text: LIV: We work perfectly together,\nme and my big sister…\pBut why did we lose again?$

replies.text: They still have each other. I hope the next revision involves the plan rather than the partnership.
A repeated result is a reason to examine which part of the approach has stayed the same.
They should change something useful, not decide the friendship itself was the mistake.
Sometimes it helps to stop rehearsing the whole piece and listen to the bit where it keeps coming apart.
I hope they take a break before trying to solve it while both are upset.
Another difficult performance calls for a useful note, not a declaration that the company is doomed.
They are allowed to feel disappointed without turning it against one another.
I would look for the same failure occurring twice. That is more useful than starting everything over blindly.
A patient conversation between them may do more good than another immediate challenge.
I hope they keep some confidence in each other while changing the parts that need work.
I would compare this attempt with the last one before deciding that nothing improved.

contexts.subject: Marcos gained listeners while playing guitar privately and wonders about going professional.

Route103_Text_MarcosPostBattle.text: I was playing my guitar where few\npeople were around, but a lot of fans\lhave gathered.\pHeh, maybe I should turn pro.$

replies.text: He went looking for somewhere quiet and accidentally acquired an audience. A very musical navigation error.
People stopping to listen is encouraging. I hope he decides what he wants from the music himself.
He can enjoy being heard without deciding his entire future this afternoon.
I would like to hear what he was playing before he noticed everyone listening.
I hope he keeps some time to play simply because he enjoys it.
An accidental audience is a lovely review. It is not yet a complete employment contract.
I hope the attention feels good to him, rather than making his quiet place feel borrowed.
He should learn what professional work involves before mistaking encouragement for the whole plan.
Something he enjoyed alone has become something he can share. He gets to choose what happens next.
I hope he can hear his own preferences as clearly as the applause.
I would like to record a little performance if he actually wanted it recorded.

contexts.subject: Miguel calls his Pokemon darling even while it has fainted.

Route103_Text_MiguelPostBattle.text: My delightful POKéMON looks darling\neven when it's fainted!$

replies.text: It can remain adorable on the way to getting some care. I suggest making that the next activity.
Affection is good. Attending to the Pokemon's condition should accompany it.
I hope admiration is followed promptly by looking after the partner who needs help.
It is nice to love a Pokemon through a loss. I would also like it to feel better.
It needs care more urgently than another compliment right now.
The performer deserves a comfortable recovery before the audience supplies further reviews.
I hope being loved means being noticed when something is wrong, too.
The affection is clear. Now I would like to see the practical response to the damage.
Care should do something for the one receiving it.
I would rather hear how comfortable the Pokemon is than how lovely it still looks.
This is a good time to put the attention into helping, rather than admiring.

contexts.subject: Miguel says his Pokemon becomes more adorable as they spend time together.

Route103_Text_MiguelRematchPostBattle.text: The more I spend time with it,\nthe more adorable my POKéMON becomes.$

replies.text: The Pokemon has discovered the most reliable beauty treatment: being someone's favorite.
Familiarity gives him more little things to notice and enjoy.
It is good when spending time together makes the ordinary parts matter more.
I like how a familiar face can become more interesting the longer you know it.
I hope the Pokemon feels that affection in its everyday care.
A long-running role with an increasingly enthusiastic audience of one.
I understand that. Knowing somebody gives you more reasons to be fond of them.
He has made a strong case for actually spending time with a partner.
Love can keep becoming more particular as you learn someone.
The best details are often the ones a first glance would have missed.
That is why I like taking another picture years later. You know what to notice differently.

contexts.subject: Pete understands wanting to Surf with a particularly trusted Pokemon.

Route103_Text_PetePostBattle.text: Oh, I understand where you're coming\nfrom now.\pIf I had a POKéMON that trusty,\nI'd want to SURF on it, too!$

replies.text: A trustworthy partner does make the sea look rather more inviting. I would still secure the sandwiches.
Trust matters when we depend on a partner so directly. It should be supported by preparation and care.
I like hearing the partnership noticed, rather than only the distance we can travel.
It must feel different to cross the water with someone whose movements you already know.
I hope the Pokemon gets the same confidence that we will look after it in return.
The journey has a companion built into it. That is a rather lovely reason to go.
I would like to feel that secure beside the water.
Trust and a well-secured bag seem like an excellent combination for the crossing.
Depending on someone should make us attentive to them, not forgetful of their effort.
It is nice when somebody notices what makes a partnership feel comfortable.
I would like a memory of the crossing that includes the Pokemon doing the carrying.

contexts.subject: Rhett asks whether we like cramped quarters.

Route103_Text_RhettPostBattle.text: Do you like cramped quarters\nlike this?$

replies.text: I prefer my personal space to include a little room for the word personal.
Enough space to move safely is a useful feature in almost any activity.
I like having room to step back when I need it.
A quiet small room can be lovely. A crowded one is quite a different instrument.
I would rather everybody have somewhere comfortable to put themselves.
Intimate staging is best arranged with the consent of the entire cast.
I would like to choose when the walls are close to me.
I usually discover a small room's limitations with my elbows and a toolbox.
A little space can make it easier to be comfortable with other people.
I would rather not arrive at a doorway already negotiating whose shoulder goes first.
Sometimes a narrow view is interesting. I prefer to photograph it without being trapped inside it.

contexts.subject: Billy wants to leave footprints all over the sand but the sea erases them.

Route104_Text_BillyPostBattle.text: I want to leave my footprints in\nthe sand everywhere, but they\ldisappear quickly…$

replies.text: The beach has an extremely efficient tidying policy. Billy seems less enthusiastic about it.
The tide changes the surface continuously. A temporary mark can still tell us that someone was there.
The walk mattered even if the sand did not keep a record.
I like that the next person gets a fresh stretch of beach to begin on.
I hope he enjoys making the footprints while they are his to look at.
A performance that the sea insists on resetting between audiences.
Something does not have to stay forever to be worth doing.
If he wants a lasting record, the beach is a rather uncooperative material.
The sea can change the trace without taking away the day he had here.
I would enjoy the pattern before asking it to last.
A picture could keep the footprints without asking the tide to change its habits.

contexts.subject: Our rival praises our handling of Pokemon and points to Briney as an example of friendship.

Route104_Text_BrendanPostBattle.text:
BRENDAN: You've gotten pretty decent
at handling POKéMON.\pBut, you know, you shouldn't just be
making POKéMON battle.\pLike MR. BRINEY, it's important to
become friends with your POKéMON.$

Route104_Text_MayPostBattle.text:
MAY: I can tell you've gotten pretty
good with the way you handle POKéMON.\pBut instead of only making them
battle, you should be like MR. BRINEY.\pIt's important to become friends with
POKéMON, too.$

replies.text: Briney and Peeko have become the local example of doing this properly. I think they would enjoy hearing that.
Skill and friendship should support each other. It is good advice to keep beside the praise.
Our team deserves a life with us outside the moments when we need to win.
I like the part where people remember how somebody treats their partner between adventures.
Meals, quiet company, noticing little needs. Friendship gets built in those ordinary parts too.
Briney has supplied a convincing example without needing to make a speech about it himself.
It is a relief to hear somebody say that being good together matters beyond a result.
A partnership that works needs care as well as an effective plan.
The trust we rely on should also be something our Pokemon get to enjoy.
I hope we are remembered kindly by the ones traveling beside us.
I would like our record of the journey to include ordinary happy days with the team.

contexts.subject: Cindy links hello and goodbye and hopes we meet again.

Route104_Text_CindyPostBattle.text: “Hello” is the beginning of “good-bye.”\nI hope we meet again.$

replies.text: I was prepared for hello to begin a conversation, not ambush me with the entire concept of leaving.
A brief meeting can still give people a reason to welcome the next one.
I hope we do meet again. It is nice to leave someone with a reason to smile.
A good goodbye can leave a little room for the next hello.
I hope she has plenty of pleasant company between now and then.
An unexpectedly melancholy opening, followed by a very agreeable proposal for a sequel.
Saying goodbye does not make meeting someone a mistake.
I like an arrangement that leaves the possibility of checking in later.
A meeting can be worth having even when you cannot keep it still.
I hope she remembers the pleasant part of the encounter while she waits for another.
I would like to hear what changed for her when we next come through.

contexts.subject: Darian complains that Magikarp does not live up to its impressive name.

Route104_Text_DarianPostBattle.text: Hey, MAGIKARP, you sure don't live up\nto your name, do you?$

replies.text: The Pokemon did not choose its name. It would like its performance review adjusted accordingly.
A name is a poor basis for setting a partner's abilities. He should learn what Magikarp can actually do.
He has the Pokemon he has, not the one a name persuaded him to imagine.
I hope he finds something to like about the real partner in front of him.
Magikarp deserves care without first having to satisfy an advertising promise.
The performer has been blamed for the title. I would take that complaint to whoever wrote the poster.
It is difficult to live comfortably beside somebody else's disappointment.
He should begin with the actual specifications, rather than what the label suggested.
A partner is more than the expectations someone brought to meeting it.
I would like Magikarp to have someone interested in who it is today.
I would rather record what Magikarp does than what someone insists it ought to do.

contexts.subject: Gina praises our strength and resolves to train more.

Route104_Text_GinaPostBattle.text: GINA: You are strong!\nWe have to train lots more!$

replies.text: She has turned the result into a plan. I hope the plan also contains a snack break.
Training is useful when it has a purpose. I hope she notices which part she wants to improve.
I like that she can respect our team and still feel hopeful about hers.
That sounds like a good note to leave the battle on.
I hope the whole team gets some rest before the next attempt.
An encouraging review and a decision to rehearse. A very healthy response to a difficult performance.
It is nice to hear determination that does not need an excuse attached to the loss.
I would turn that enthusiasm into one clear adjustment before the next practice.
A loss can leave room for admiration and hope at the same time.
I hope she keeps that generosity toward her own team while they learn.
I would enjoy seeing what she does differently when we next meet.

contexts.subject: Haley warns against letting other people make decisions we must live with.

Route104_Text_HaleyPostBattle.text: If you're faced with a decision and\nyou let someone else choose for you,\lyou will regret it, however things\lturn out.$

replies.text: I can supply opinions. I would prefer not to accidentally become the person who chose your entire afternoon.
Advice can clarify a decision without taking ownership of it away from the person affected.
I can stand beside you while you choose. You should still get to choose.
It helps to hear your own reasons clearly beneath everybody else's suggestions.
I want my advice to make things easier for you, not make you feel that you owe me a particular answer.
An adviser is not automatically entitled to the leading role.
It can be difficult to tell what you want when you are busy trying not to disappoint someone.
I would rather explain the trade-offs than pretend there is only one respectable answer.
A kind relationship should leave room for a decision the other person would not have made.
People can mean well and still be very loud about the wrong future for you.
I would like to hear what matters to you before offering a direction.

contexts.subject: Ivan became so absorbed in fishing that he neglected raising his Pokemon.

Route104_Text_IvanPostBattle.text: I got too into fishing.\nI forgot I had to raise my POKéMON…$

replies.text: The fishing has been excellent at catching his entire attention.
Enjoying an activity should not make a partner's ordinary needs disappear from the plan.
He has noticed the problem. The useful next step is looking after the Pokemon, not only feeling bad about it.
It is easy for a favorite thing to fill more of the day than you meant to give it.
I hope he makes some quiet time for his team before going back to the water.
The supporting cast still needs attention while the main character pursues a hobby.
I hope his Pokemon get more than a guilty apology out of this realization.
A routine might help him remember the work that does not announce itself as loudly as a bite.
What depends on us deserves a place in the day, even when something else is exciting.
He can keep the hobby and become more thoughtful about the people sharing it with him.
I would like to hear what he changes afterward. Noticing is the beginning of the useful part.

contexts.subject: Mia wants to train her team to become strong like ours.

Route104_Text_MiaPostBattle.text: MIA: We will train our POKéMON more\nand be strong like you.$

replies.text: I hope she finds her own version of strong. Ours currently includes a surprising amount of walking.
It is good to have an example, and equally useful to understand what makes that example work.
I hope she sees things worth learning without deciding her own team is somehow wrong.
It is lovely to know our journey has given somebody else a little encouragement.
I hope they are patient with one another while they get there.
She has found an inspiring performance. I hope the rehearsal becomes something she enjoys for itself too.
I hope she discovers things her own team does that are worth being proud of already.
Learning from a result is useful. Copying only the visible parts usually misses the interesting work.
Someone else's achievement can open a possibility without having to become an exact blueprint.
I would like her to feel proud of the progress while it is still progress.
I hope we meet again and get to notice how far her team has come.

contexts.subject: Winston reflects that some things, including Pokemon, cannot be bought.

Route104_Text_WinstonPostBattle.text: There are some things money can't buy.\nThat's POKéMON…$

replies.text: I am glad the money has discovered the limits of its conversational authority.
A genuine partnership requires things a transaction cannot supply on its own.
Trust takes care and time, however impressive someone's wallet is.
It is nice to hear someone noticing what a relationship asks beyond acquiring things.
Having resources can help with care. Deciding to give that care is still a choice somebody has to make.
An expensive education in the existence of other kinds of value.
I hope the thought stays with him after the disappointment wears off.
Good equipment helps. It does not do the work of understanding a partner.
Being able to have something is different from learning to live well with it.
I would like his Pokemon to receive affection that is not measured by what they cost.
I would rather hear what his team has taught him than what it would have been priced at.

contexts.subject: After successfully giving Tea, the woman praises hot tea for thirst.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_1F_Text_Nothing.text: Nothing beats thirst like some hot\nTEA.\pIt really is the best.$

replies.text: She has strong opinions about tea. Luckily, they come with actual tea.
A generous recommendation, backed by a sample. Excellent procedure.
She noticed we were passing through and gave us something useful.
There is something reassuring about how certain she is of a simple pleasure.
Good tea and a warm welcome. That is a respectable house specialty.
Her argument has a fragrant supporting exhibit. I find it persuasive.
The world briefly became a little warmer. Tea does that sometimes.
No elaborate sales pitch. She just handed us the solution.
A small hot cup can make quite a large invitation.
She knows her favorite and shares it without making a performance of it.
I like that she welcomed a traveler with something she enjoys herself.

contexts.subject: The tea woman enjoys her Pokemon company; Meowth brings home money.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_1F_Text_MyDearM.text: My dear POKéMON keep me company.\nMEOWTH even brings money home!$

replies.text: Meowth contributes to the household budget? I owe several plush toys an awkward conversation.
Companionship and an income. Meowth has a remarkably broad role here.
They keep her company. The money sounds like a pleasant extra.
She sounds proud of them in a very familiar, everyday way.
That Meowth pays its way. Mine would probably invoice me for lunch.
A devoted household, with one unusually enterprising member.
A quiet room full of company. That sounds like a decent life.
Meowth brings money home? Better accounting than some businesses.
Perhaps Meowth considers coins a perfectly ordinary affection.
She says dear Pokemon first and money second. Good priorities.
I wonder where Meowth goes on those little earning expeditions.

contexts.subject: The woman asks about Pallet and mentions Daisy buys tea in Celadon.

CeladonCity_Condominiums_1F_Text_DaisyCo.text:
Oh, hello, dearie.
Did you enjoy my TEA?\pBy the way, dear. Are you, by any
chance, from PALLET TOWN?\pA girl from PALLET TOWN, DAISY,
she enjoys TEA every day.\pShe visits the CELADON DEPT. STORE
to buy some TEA.$

replies.text: Daisy has a tea route! That is a very civilized kind of adventure.
A daily habit explains why the shop and Daisy are familiar to her.
Nice to hear a familiar name so far from Pallet.
She remembered Daisy through something small. Those details stay with people.
A favorite tea is a good reason to make a regular trip.
A little thread from Pallet turns up here, smelling faintly of tea.
People leave traces in ordinary places. Sometimes the trace is a shopping list.
Daisy found a dependable supplier. An underrated accomplishment.
The teacup seems to know more people than I do.
She remembers what Daisy enjoys. That is a sweet sort of familiarity.
Celadon must feel less anonymous when somebody remembers your usual purchase.

contexts.subject: The department store receptionist directs us to its layout board.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_1F_Text_Welc.text: Hello!\nWelcome to CELADON DEPT. STORE.\pThe board on the right describes\nthe store layout.$

replies.text: A whole building of shopping, with instructions. They anticipated my wandering.
The directory should save us several unnecessary journeys between floors.
Check the board before we haul the team up five flights.
That was a clear welcome. I appreciate knowing where to start.
A directory first, shopping second. My feet support this arrangement.
The grand expedition begins by reading the board immediately to our right.
A map of temptation. At least the floors are labeled.
Good signage! The least glamorous part of a building doing important work.
So many floors, and only one pair of feet apiece.
She points people toward what they need. That is good service.
I wonder which floor gets the most lost visitors.

contexts.subject: A shopper studies Super Repel and compares it with ordinary Repel.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_2F_Text_Supe.text: SUPER REPEL keeps weak POKéMON at\nbay…\pHmm, it's a more powerful REPEL.$

replies.text: The name does seem fairly confident about being better.
Comparing the labels is sensible. Similar packaging can hide useful differences.
Worth checking before paying extra for the word Super.
They are taking their time with the choice. That seems reasonable.
Buy the version that suits the walk, rather than the loudest name.
A product named Super has narrowly survived its first critical review.
The promise of fewer interruptions has an understandable appeal.
A comparison shopper! Finally, somebody reads the specifications.
Some journeys call for a little more distance between strangers.
They are reading instead of buying by the color of the bottle. Sensible.
Everyone prepares differently for the same patch of tall grass.

contexts.subject: A shopper recommends carrying Revives for long outings.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_2F_Text_BuyR.text: For long outings, you should buy\nREVIVE.$

replies.text: Long outing supplies: shoes, water, and a way to rescue the plan.
A contingency item becomes more useful as the distance to a Center grows.
Good advice. A long road is a poor place to discover an empty pocket.
They sound like they have had a journey go wrong before.
A little preparation keeps a difficult outing from becoming a miserable one.
One prefers an uneventful journey, but packs for a less considerate author.
An unexciting purchase can be the best one by the end of the day.
Spare capacity for a bad day. I approve of that design principle.
A way back onto your feet is worth carrying.
Practical advice, delivered without inspecting our entire bag. Appreciated.
That sounds like advice somebody learned a long walk from town.

contexts.subject: The clerk wonders why Lance repeatedly buys identical capes.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_2F_Text_Lanc.text: We have a customer, LANCE, who\noccasionally comes.\pHe always buys capes.\pI wonder… Does he have many\nidentical capes at home?$

replies.text: Emergency cape. Spare cape. Cape for when the emergency cape gets dramatic.
Repeated purchases suggest wear, preference, or an exceptionally narrow wardrobe.
Find something that works. Buy a spare. I understand him.
Having one reliable look must make mornings easier.
Even capes need laundry days. Probably very inconvenient laundry days.
A man cannot let his signature silhouette be defeated by a washing line.
Perhaps every cape is different in ways only he can bear to explain.
Rotation reduces wear! Though cape storage must be a peculiar engineering problem.
A cupboard full of the same shadow. Oddly comforting.
Consistency is a style choice. So is having absolutely no backup look.
The staff remember his capes before anything else. That is quite an impression.

contexts.subject: A shopper explains original trainer registration and ID numbers.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_3F_Text_OTSt.text: Captured POKéMON are registered\nwith an ID No. and the OT.\pOT stands for “Original TRAINER” -\nthe TRAINER that caught it first.$

replies.text: A Pokemon can have a long history before it meets us. A little label remembers the start.
The registration preserves provenance even when the Pokemon changes companions.
Useful to know where a partner came from. Useful to treat it well now, too.
A name in the record is a small piece of somebody else's journey.
Records help, especially when a Pokemon has traveled through several hands.
Every arrival has a first chapter, even when we enter much later.
A beginning that does not vanish when the next part starts. I like that.
An ID makes the record traceable. Clear labeling earns its keep again.
Names can travel without their owners. These ones follow Pokemon.
A useful detail to check when meeting a traded partner.
I wonder how many different towns a traded Pokemon remembers.

contexts.subject: A shopper is excited to trade Haunter for a friend's Kangaskhan.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_3F_Text_Budd.text: All right!\pMy buddy's going to trade me his\nKANGASKHAN for my HAUNTER!$

replies.text: Both friends found a Pokemon they want. That is a promising exchange.
A trade between friends offers the reassuring possibility of future updates.
As long as both know what they are agreeing to, sounds fair.
The excitement makes the whole shop feel a little less impersonal.
They sound pleased with the arrangement. Good to settle that before trading.
Two collections take an interesting turn, with a handshake in the middle.
A friend is a comforting person to trust with a familiar Pokemon.
A mutually useful swap. Those are remarkably satisfying when they work out.
Two companions finding different doors to walk through.
Knowing what your friend wants makes a good trade much easier.
I would be curious to hear how both Pokemon settle into the change.

contexts.subject: The Haunter collector is surprised that the traded Haunter evolved.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_3F_Text_Haun.text: Come on, HAUNTER!\pI love HAUNTER!\nI collect them!\pHuh?\pHAUNTER turned into a different\nPOKéMON while being traded!$

replies.text: They ordered a Haunter and received a surprise with a much larger grin.
The trade triggered evolution. Their collection plan omitted an important variable.
Still their new partner. Just came with an unexpected change.
They sounded so certain a moment ago. That must be a lot to take in.
Give the new arrival a chance before deciding the trade went wrong.
The collector's carefully arranged expectation has acquired teeth.
A ghost found a way to surprise the person specifically collecting ghosts.
Unexpected behavior! Useful discovery, unfortunate timing for the collection.
Even a familiar ghost has another shape tucked away.
They loved the look they expected. I wonder how this new look will grow on them.
That reaction tells me nobody warned them what trading could do.

contexts.subject: A shopper explains using ID numbers to identify traded Pokemon.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_3F_Text_CanI.text: You can identify POKéMON you get\nin trades by their ID Numbers.$

replies.text: A tiny number doing a great deal of remembering.
Consistent identifiers prevent confusion when names or ownership change.
Worth checking the record before mixing up two partners.
It is good that something can keep their histories distinct.
Careful records matter when several similar Pokemon arrive together.
A modest string of digits keeps an elaborate case of mistaken identity at bay.
A number cannot tell the whole story, but it can keep two stories apart.
Labels that survive a handoff! Someone thought about the awkward cases.
A small mark can follow a very long journey.
Especially useful when everyone has named their Pokemon something fashionable.
The number is one way to trace where a new partner began.

contexts.subject: A shopper chooses a popular Poke Doll as a present for his girlfriend.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_4F_Text_Gett.text: I'm getting a present for my\ngirlfriend.\pI guess a POKé DOLL will be it.\nIt's the popular thing.$

replies.text: A doll is a good start. Knowing which one she likes would be an even better start.
Popularity is information about many people. Her preferences would be better data.
Ask what she likes. Saves a second trip.
He wants to choose well. I hope he remembers something she has actually mentioned.
A present lands better when there is a little of the person in the choice.
The popular choice has volunteered as a substitute for romantic research.
A small, soft offering. There are worse ways to be unsure.
A tiny bit of user research could make this a much stronger selection.
Perhaps she has already pointed at the answer in a shop window.
Popular is fine. Her favorite color would make it feel meant for her.
I wonder whether she collects them or whether this will be her first.

contexts.subject: A shopper explains distracting wild Pokemon with a Poke Doll to escape.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_4F_Text_CanR.text: I heard something useful.\pIf a wild POKéMON appears, you can\ndistract it with a POKé DOLL.\pYou can run away while the wild\nPOKéMON is distracted.$

replies.text: The doll has a dangerous second career. I thought it only sat on shelves.
A distraction can create enough time to withdraw without another attack.
An escape option is useful. No need to win every encounter.
Leaving safely sounds better than pressing a battle the team cannot manage.
One more sensible thing to carry when the route is unfamiliar.
A plush decoy. The gift department has concealed a tactical division.
A soft toy buying a hard exit. Unexpectedly practical.
Simple distraction, immediate retreat. Elegant, if rough on the doll.
A little false friend left behind so the real ones can leave.
Cute and useful. A surprisingly strong argument for shelf space.
I would never have guessed that use from looking at the display.

contexts.subject: A customer explains the different stat enhancers sold on this floor.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_5F_Text_Expl.text:
POKéMON stat enhancers can be
bought only here.\pHP UP increases the base HP of a
POKéMON.\pCALCIUM raises the base SP. ATK
stat of one POKéMON.\pZINC boosts the base SP. DEF stat
of one POKéMON.\pCARBOS enhances the base SPEED
stat.$

replies.text: That is a lot of bottles to keep straight. My shopping list needs a shopping list.
Different supplements target different attributes. The labels deserve careful attention.
Know what the team needs before buying the expensive bottle.
They have clearly spent time understanding the differences.
The right purchase matters more than coming away with a heavy bag.
An entire shelf of improvements, each with its own rather confident name.
So many tiny bottles promising to make a difference. Choose carefully.
Specific effects, clear categories. I could spend far too long comparing these.
A little bottle is still a choice about what you want to grow.
Good that they explained the differences. Those labels are not exactly intuitive.
The fifth floor attracts some very deliberate planners.

contexts.subject: A shopper describes Protein for Attack and Iron for Defense.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_5F_Text_Here.text:
I'm here for POKéMON stat
enhancers.\pPROTEIN increases the base ATTACK
power.\pIRON increases the base DEFENSE
stat.$

replies.text: Protein and Iron. The shopping basket sounds tougher than I do.
Attack and defense call for different purchases. Specific goals simplify the choice.
Hit harder or hold up longer. Depends what the team is missing.
They seem to have a reason for coming to this particular shelf.
A label saying Protein still does not make it a meal.
Two very different approaches to surviving the same difficult afternoon.
Strength and endurance in neighboring bottles. A tidy little rivalry.
Useful distinction. More force and more resistance solve different problems.
One bottle for striking, another for weathering the strike.
They know what they came for. Dangerous shopping skill in a store this large.
I wonder whether they buy for one partner or plan for a whole team.

contexts.subject: After receiving water and giving TM16, the girl explains Light Screen.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_Roof_Text_Ex.text: TM16 contains LIGHT SCREEN.\pIt's a move that weakens the power\nof special attacks by your foe.$

replies.text: We brought water; she brought protection from special attacks. Strong picnic arrangement.
She knows exactly what her gift does. A thoughtful exchange.
Light Screen could keep the team standing through a rough special attack.
Her thank-you was generous. I like that she explained it, too.
A bottle of water turned into something that can help the whole team.
An unexpectedly practical flourish to a very ordinary kindness.
Clear water, a barrier of light. She has a consistent aesthetic.
A defensive option from a rooftop errand. Productive detour!
We eased her thirst; she gave us a little shelter.
She was prepared to thank somebody properly. That is rather sweet.
That small exchange gave us more than I expected when we walked upstairs.

contexts.subject: After receiving Soda Pop and giving TM20, the girl explains Safeguard.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_Roof_Text_Ex.text: TM20 contains SAFEGUARD.\pIt's a move that prevents status\nproblems among your POKéMON.$

replies.text: Soda for Safeguard. Fizzy drinks have become a strategic resource.
Preventing status problems can preserve several turns of a difficult battle.
Useful cover against tricks that stop a partner from acting.
She made sure we knew why the gift could help.
A grateful explanation beats just handing over a mysterious disc.
A fizzy interlude concludes with an unusually sensible defensive recommendation.
A little protection against unpleasant surprises. Good rooftop luck.
Prevention! Fixing a problem before it appears is deeply satisfying.
A sweet drink purchased a small ward against trouble.
She traded us something useful rather than something she merely wanted gone.
Who expects a lesson in status protection beside a vending machine?

contexts.subject: After receiving Lemonade and giving TM33, the girl explains Reflect.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_Roof_Text_Ex.text: TM33 contains REFLECT.\pIt's a move that weakens the power\nof physical attacks by your foe.$

replies.text: Lemonade in, defensive wall out. This roof has excellent exchange rates.
Reflect reduces the threat of physical attacks. A useful addition to our options.
A little more room to take a hit and keep going. Worth remembering.
She sounded happy to share something that matters to her team.
A refreshing drink and a helpful thank-you. Both sides did well.
Lemonade has purchased us a rather more durable kind of refreshment.
There is an odd gentleness to a gift that softens a blow.
Physical protection from a small disc! Nice payoff for a drink run.
She answered a small kindness with a little wall of light.
A good gift comes with enough explanation to actually use it.
The rooftop crowd knows more about battle support than I expected.

contexts.subject: The girl cannot give her reward because the bag has no room.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_Roof_Text_Do.text: You don't have space for this!$

replies.text: We found room for generosity but forgot a pocket for the reply.
The reward could not fit. We should avoid assuming the exchange completed normally.
Bag is full. Sort it before trying to carry anything else.
She did try to give us something. It is awkward when the bag gets in the way.
A little sorting would have helped before making the exchange.
A charming transaction has encountered the immovable force of packed luggage.
A full bag can make even a thank-you complicated.
Capacity limit. Predictable in theory, annoying at exactly this moment.
The gift has reached a door that opens onto a wall of belongings.
Our bag has chosen an unfortunate moment to reject accessories.
That is a different ending than the cheerful exchange she had in mind.

contexts.subject: The girl declines a drink whose corresponding reward was already claimed.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_Roof_Text_Im.text: No, thank you!\nI'm not thirsty after all!$

replies.text: The thirst has withdrawn its application. Fair enough.
She declined. There is no reason to press the offer.
Keep the drink for later. She said no.
At least she let us know before we handed it over.
Another time, perhaps. A drink keeps better than an awkward insistence.
A sudden revision in the rooftop thirst forecast.
Even a simple offer can reach its natural ending.
Request canceled. Conveniently, the drink is still usable.
Thirst comes and goes. The bottle can wait.
She changed her answer politely. That is enough explanation.
Interesting how quickly that request disappeared once we offered something.

contexts.subject: The girl says she wants a drink when we are carrying none.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_Roof_Text_Im.text: I'm thirsty!\nI want something to drink!$

replies.text: She has identified the problem. The vending machines seem to have anticipated it.
A straightforward request, with a likely source of drinks nearby.
If we buy one, do it because we choose to.
She is being very direct about what she needs.
A rooftop in the sun is a sensible place to want a cold drink.
The roof presents a thirst problem alongside several coin-operated answers.
A very small emergency, stated with complete conviction.
Demand and supply are standing impressively close together.
The machines hum, and someone nearby wishes for a drink.
She has made her priorities unusually easy to understand.
I wonder how long she has been standing beside those machines.

contexts.subject: A trainer complains that his trainer sister is immature.

CeladonCity_DepartmentStore_Roof_Text_My.text: My sister is a TRAINER, believe it\nor not.\pBut, she's so immature, she drives\nme nuts!$

replies.text: Siblings can apparently detect immaturity from several floors away.
Being a trainer does not make someone mature in every other respect.
Sounds like siblings. A badge will not settle that argument.
She may be different around him than around her Pokemon.
A family outing can test patience more thoroughly than a battle.
A brother files his official rooftop grievance. The sister has not been called to testify.
Family has a way of remembering your least dignified moments.
Training skills and sibling diplomacy clearly need separate practice.
He knows exactly which little things she does to annoy him.
He says that with the exhaustion only a sibling can earn.
We have heard his side. I suspect she could offer a lively response.

contexts.subject: The hotel clerk explains this is a human hotel and all rooms are full.

CeladonCity_Hotel_Text_ThisHotelIsForPeo.text: POKéMON?\nNo, this is a hotel for people.\pWe're full up, unfortunately.$

replies.text: A bed for people! Tragically, all the people arrived before us.
Different accommodation, same capacity problem. There are no vacancies.
Full up. We will need another place to rest.
An easy mistake from outside. At least they explained kindly.
A room would have been nice. We can still find somewhere to sit.
Human lodging exists, but has declined to demonstrate its comforts today.
A building full of occupied beds. Somehow that makes my feet more tired.
Correct service, zero available capacity. That answers both questions.
Every room already holds someone else's little evening.
The clerk has probably had to explain that distinction quite often.
Busy hotel. Celadon seems to attract visitors from everywhere.

contexts.subject: A woman enjoys Celadon on vacation with her brother and boyfriend.

CeladonCity_Hotel_Text_OnVacationWithBro.text: I'm on vacation with my brother and\nboyfriend.\pCELADON is such a pretty city!$

replies.text: She brought two favorite people to a pretty city. Ambitious travel planning.
A mixed group can enjoy the same city for quite different reasons.
She is having a good time. That is what the trip is for.
It is nice to hear somebody enjoying the city without being in a hurry.
A holiday with family and someone you love sounds worth planning.
Celadon has acquired a party with three perspectives on the itinerary.
She sounds happily oblivious to any complications. A useful holiday skill.
Three people, one itinerary. Hope somebody built in flexible time.
A pretty city becomes a different place with familiar company.
She looks pleased with her arrangements. I respect that confidence.
I wonder which place she wants to show them first.

contexts.subject: The boyfriend wonders why his girlfriend brought her brother on vacation.

CeladonCity_Hotel_Text_WhyDidSheBringBro.text: Why?\nWhy did she bring her brother?$

replies.text: He packed for a date and discovered a family excursion.
Their expectations for the trip appear to differ substantially.
He should ask her. Quietly resenting the brother will not help.
That sounds like a conversation they should have between themselves.
A surprise extra guest changes a holiday faster than bad weather.
The romantic itinerary has encountered an unscheduled sibling.
He is mourning a trip that apparently existed only in his own planning.
This is why the passenger list belongs near the top of the plan.
Three travelers, and one imagined table for two.
They really should have compared their ideas of a romantic getaway.
Same reservation, very different expectations. That could be a long holiday.

contexts.subject: The brother is delighted his sister brought him on vacation.

CeladonCity_Hotel_Text_SisBroughtMeOnVac.text: Yippee! I'm on vacation!\nMy sis brought me along! Awesome!$

replies.text: At least one person has no complaints about the guest list!
For him, the arrangement is an uncomplicated success.
Kid got a holiday with his sister. Hard to fault that excitement.
He sounds so glad she thought to include him.
Being invited along can mean a lot when you are the younger one.
Our third traveler awards the trip an entirely unqualified review.
A little joy, completely untroubled by romantic scheduling.
One satisfied passenger! That is useful feedback for the organizer.
His holiday has begun exactly where the others' argument might.
He is having the time he was promised. That is quite sweet.
I like how differently all three people describe the same vacation.

contexts.subject: The restaurant worker says staff are taking a break.

CeladonCity_Restaurant_Text_TakingBreakR.text: Hi!\pSorry, but we're taking a break\nright now.$

replies.text: The people who serve lunch also need lunch. A sound arrangement.
Scheduled rest is part of operating a restaurant sustainably.
They are on break. We can come back.
They sounded polite about it. No reason to make their rest awkward.
Good. The kitchen deserves time to breathe between orders.
Even the grand business of feeding strangers requires an intermission.
For once, a closed service means somebody gets to sit down.
Maintenance includes the people doing the work. Easy to forget.
The room can be quiet while the hands that feed it rest.
A short explanation and a proper boundary. Nicely handled.
It must feel different in here when the lunch rush finally stops.

contexts.subject: A diner says weak Pokemon lead to frequent drugstore visits.

CeladonCity_Restaurant_Text_OftenGoToDru.text: My POKéMON are weak, so I often\nhave to go to the DRUGSTORE.$

replies.text: The drugstore knows them by now. I hope the team gets some quiet afternoons too.
Frequent recovery needs may suggest adjusting the training plan as well as buying supplies.
If every trip ends at the drugstore, ease up on the team.
That sounds tiring for both the trainer and the Pokemon.
Supplies help, but a gentler pace could save them a lot of trouble.
The local shop prospers while this trainer's itinerary limps along.
A routine built around getting hurt could use a small revision.
Repeated repairs usually mean it is time to check how something is being used.
Perhaps the route needs to get shorter before the shopping list does.
They sound resigned to it. A change of plan might suit everyone better.
I wonder whether they have tried a route better suited to their team.

contexts.subject: A diner whispers a rumor about a basement beneath the Game Corner.

CeladonCity_Restaurant_Text_PsstBasement.text: Psst! There's a basement under the\nGAME CORNER, I hear.$

replies.text: A basement rumor delivered at whisper volume. That always makes the stairs sound worse.
A useful lead, though a rumor still needs confirmation.
Worth remembering. Do not walk into an unknown basement unprepared.
They lowered their voice before saying it. That makes me a little uneasy.
A place can look cheerful upstairs and still have trouble underneath.
The local gossip has developed an underground branch.
A bright room overhead does not tell us much about what lies below it.
Could be ordinary storage. Could be something worth checking carefully.
The city has another layer people only discuss in whispers.
That was a very deliberate whisper for a very public dining room.
I wonder how the rumor started, and who has actually been down there.

contexts.subject: After giving away his Coin Case, the ruined gambler admits chasing losses.

CeladonCity_Restaurant_Text_ThoughtIdWin.text: I always thought I was going to\nwin it back…$

replies.text: That sounds like a very expensive tomorrow that never arrived.
Expecting the next attempt to erase previous losses can sustain a damaging cycle.
Good that he stopped. Losing more would not fix what is gone.
He says it so quietly now. It must hurt to understand it afterward.
I am glad he is stepping away. He deserves a steadier evening.
A cruel promise: one more try, and the whole story will turn around.
He kept paying for an ending the machines did not owe him.
Past losses cannot improve the next result. A brutal lesson to buy.
A small box of coins can become a very deep hole.
That is a hard thing to admit to a stranger. No jokes at his expense.
His explanation tells us much more than the room's gossip about him did.

contexts.subject: A shopper looks for X Attack to raise Attack during battle.

CinnabarIsland_Mart_Text_DontTheyHaveXAt.text: Don't they have X ATTACK?\pI like it because it raises the\nATTACK stat in battle.$

replies.text: They came for one very specific kind of extra oomph.
They want a temporary battle enhancement, rather than a permanent training change.
Worth checking stock before building a whole plan around it.
Knowing the exact item must make the rest of the shelf easier to ignore.
A short shopping list can still be frustrating when the one item is missing.
The offensive strategy has paused for a disagreement with the inventory.
One absent bottle, one interrupted plan for violence.
Specific requirements meet uncertain stock. Classic supply problem.
An empty space on a shelf can stop quite a confident plan.
They know what they want. The shop has yet to cooperate.
I wonder how often visiting trainers ask for that particular item.

contexts.subject: A Cinnabar shopper recommends carrying spare items for surprises.

CinnabarIsland_Mart_Text_ExtraItemsNever.text: It never hurts to have extra items.\nYou never know what might happen.$

replies.text: Extra items do hurt when the bag strap finally gives up. Still, sensible thought.
Reserves reduce uncertainty, provided we can carry them comfortably.
Keep the essentials spare. We still have to carry the bag.
It is comforting to have a little room for things going differently.
A few sensible extras can save a very inconvenient return trip.
An optimistic excursion deserves a pessimistically stocked pocket.
Spare supplies are quiet until the exact moment they become wonderful.
Redundancy! A spare can turn a failure into a brief inconvenience.
The unplanned part of a journey rarely sends a shopping list.
A useful reserve, within reason. A packed bag has opinions too.
Island shops must hear plenty of stories about forgotten supplies.

contexts.subject: A visitor speculates that the locked Gym key may be in the burned mansion.

CinnabarIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Cin.text:
I came to visit the CINNABAR GYM,
but the door is locked tight.\pThere should be a key for it
somewhere.\pCould it be in that burned-out
mansion?\pThe GYM LEADER's friend used to
live there, they say.$

replies.text: A missing key in a burned mansion. That is an unusually complicated opening time.
The mansion is a lead, though the visitor is speculating about the key.
A burned building deserves caution, even if it might hold what we need.
They came to challenge the Gym and found a very different problem.
We should prepare before searching an old damaged place.
The Gym entrance has outsourced its challenge to a rather ominous address.
A locked door points toward a burned house. This island has difficult errands.
A key search in a damaged building. Better watch where we step.
The old house is keeping more than its own doors shut.
They are careful to say could. We should remember that part.
The connection between the old resident and the Gym might be worth asking about.

contexts.subject: A visitor advises that delaying evolution can allow learning moves first.

CinnabarIsland_PokemonCenter_1F_Text_Evo.text: POKéMON can still learn techniques\nafter canceling evolution.\pEvolution can wait until new moves\nhave been learned.$

replies.text: Growing up can wait until the homework is done. Pokemon get that option!
